## Moving to Myrtle Beach Checklist: Your First 45 Days in SC
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/moving-checklist/
Summary: The deadlines and fees when you move to Myrtle Beach: license and vehicle registration in 45 days, the county vehicle tax, and the 4% residence application.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / Moving Checklist
New resident checklist, in deadline order

# Moving to Myrtle Beach: your first 45 days.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer & licensed MLO, NMLS 2721275 · Reviewed by Timmy Fredrick Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated August 25, 2026
You have 45 days to get a South Carolina license and register each car. Do the county before the DMV, budget about $305 per vehicle plus the county tax, and file the 4 percent residence application by May 31.
Ask us about a specific move Call 854.333.2135

The direct answer

## The whole move, on one screen
Each step links to its details.
1 Pack the paperwork One folder: identity, Social Security number, two address proofs. Details 2 Switch your auto insurance To a South Carolina insurer, before any office visit. Details 3 County: pay each vehicle's tax The Auditor writes the bill, the Treasurer takes payment. Details 4 DMV: license and plates About $305 per car. 45 days from the move. Details 5 File the 4 percent application By May 31, after license and plates. Roughly three to one on the tax. Details 6 Start the utilities Water wants 24 hours notice. Which electric company depends on the address. Details 7 Solve trash pickup No curbside outside city limits. Three options; know yours. Details 8 Get the parking decal Free beach parking, city residents only. Details 9 Golf cart permit $5 at the DMV, good for five years. Details 10 Register to vote, check your zones 30 days before an election. Flood and evacuation zones at the same time. Details

### The three deadlines that cost money if you miss them
First, 45 days from the day you move to get a South Carolina driver's license and to register every vehicle you own. The DMV charges about $305 per car, and the county charges its annual vehicle tax before the DMV will hand you a plate. Second, the 4 percent legal residence application for your new home, which Horry County wants by May 31; without it your first property tax bill is calculated at the 6 percent second-home rate. Third, voter registration, which closes 30 days before any election.
Devin, who wrote this page, moved here from Ohio three years ago, missed the 45 day license window, and did not learn about the free resident beach parking until his second year. This is the checklist he wishes someone had handed him.

Before the truck leaves

## What to bring, because the DMV will ask for it
Every step below asks for the same short stack of paper. Pack it in the car, not the moving truck.
Proof of who you are a certified birth certificate or an unexpired U.S. passport.
Your Social Security number. The DMV checks it electronically; the card itself is not required, but the number is.
Two proofs of your new South Carolina address, from two different organizations, dated within nine months : a lease or closing statement, a utility bill or approved application for service, a bank statement, an insurance bill, a pay stub, or the Postal Service change-of-address confirmation. One proof gets you a standard license; two get you a REAL ID at the same price.
Your out-of-state driver's license. You surrender it.
The name of an auto insurer licensed in South Carolina. Switch your policy before the DMV visit; the county wants it too.
For each vehicle the current out-of-state registration or title, and the lienholder's name if there is a loan.
If married your spouse's license and registration will be needed for the property tax application later, even if the house is in one name.

Week one

## Insurance, then the county, then the DMV: the order matters
South Carolina charges an annual property tax on cars, paid a year in advance to the county, and the DMV will not register a vehicle until it is paid. So the sequence is fixed. Get South Carolina auto insurance. Take each vehicle's registration or title and proof of your Horry County address to the county Auditor, who writes the vehicle tax notice. Pay it at the county Treasurer. Take the paid receipt to the DMV.
In Myrtle Beach the county Auditor and Treasurer are at 1201 21st Avenue North and the DMV branch is at 1200 21st Avenue North, across the street. In Little River the county office and the DMV share 107 Highway 57 North. Conway has the county offices at 1301 Second Avenue and the DMV at 4103 Highway 701 North. Offices run weekdays; the DMV opens at 8:30 and at 9:30 on Wednesdays. There is no DMV branch in Surfside, Socastee, or Carolina Forest.

### What each vehicle costs
At the DMV: a one-time $250 infrastructure maintenance fee (this is South Carolina's version of vehicle sales tax, and you pay it once, on arrival, in place of tax on a car you already own), a $15 title fee, and $40 for a plate and registration that lasts two years. That is $305 per standard passenger vehicle. Owners 65 and older pay $36 for the plate instead of $40.
At the county: the vehicle tax, which New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Ohio do not charge and which surprises almost everyone who arrives from them. It is not only cars: the county also bills boats and campers every year, so count them when you budget. Vehicles are assessed at 6 percent of value and then taxed at the local millage, and it comes due every year with the plate renewal. Horry County publishes a vehicle tax estimator on its vehicle tax page. A high-mileage discount exists, but only in the month the tax is due, so ask the Auditor about it at the counter.

### The license itself
Same visit if you brought the paperwork above. An eight-year license is $25. Expect a vision test; if your old license has been expired nine months or more, expect the knowledge and road tests too. Military members and students living here temporarily can keep their home-state license.
Buying before you move? We can time the closing around these dates.
Ask about my move Call 854.333.2135

The one that saves real money

## File the 4 percent legal residence application by May 31
This is general information, not tax or legal advice. Deadlines and required documents change. Confirm your own situation with the Horry County Auditor or a tax professional before you rely on any of it.
Horry County taxes an owner-occupied home at a 4 percent assessment and everything else at 6 percent, and the 4 percent rate also removes the school operating tax. On the same house the difference is roughly three to one. Nobody applies for you. Our Horry County property tax page has the calculator and the full explanation; here is the deadline logic.
Apply online through the county's tax-payer services page. It asks for a South Carolina driver's license or state ID for every owner-occupant and their spouse, showing the new address; South Carolina registration for every vehicle you own, showing the new address; and redacted copies of your most recent federal and state income tax returns, or an SSA-1099. If you still own a home in another state, you also send that county's tax bill showing no owner-occupied exemption there. That is why the license and registration come first: they are attachments to this form.
Horry County asks for the application by May 31 so the bill mailed in the fall prints at 4 percent. File later and you can still qualify for that year, but you will be dealing with a corrected bill or a refund instead of a right bill the first time.

### Homestead exemption at 65: not in year one
South Carolina exempts the first $50,000 of a legal residence's value for owners who are 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind. It requires the 4 percent status and one full year as a South Carolina legal resident as of December 31, so a retiree who moves this year applies for it next year, at the county Auditor.

Utilities

## Who provides what depends on which side of a line you are on
There is no single utility for the Grand Strand. Which company serves your house depends on the address, and neither electric provider publishes a street-level map. The fastest way to find out is to ask the seller for a recent bill or ask the closing attorney. Failing that, call and give them the address.

### Electricity
Two providers cover almost all of Horry County. Santee Cooper, the state-owned utility, serves the City of Myrtle Beach and the other coastal municipalities. Horry Electric Cooperative, which is member-owned, serves most of the unincorporated county, including Carolina Forest, Socastee, Longs, and the rural areas.
Both run a credit check and may want a deposit. Santee Cooper sets its deposit from the two highest consecutive bills at that address, with a floor of $100, and refunds it after 13 months of on-time payments; a prepaid option costs $70 up front and skips the deposit and credit check entirely. Horry Electric charges $35 in one-time fees to open an account, a $5 membership, a $10 application and a $20 connection, and adds a deposit only if the credit check calls for one. Both want proof you own or rent the place, so have the settlement statement or lease handy.
One thing to know before your first bill lands. On their published 2026 residential schedules, both Santee Cooper and Horry Electric Cooperative bill a demand charge as well as the power you use, which means part of what you pay is set by your single highest hour of use rather than your monthly total. The peak window is 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. from April through October and 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. from November through March. Running several heavy appliances at once inside that window sets a charge that applies to the whole month, so it is worth spreading the load. Our cost of living page has the rates.

### Water and sewer
Outside the city limits, most of the coast is served by Grand Strand Water & Sewer Authority, which asks for 24 hours notice before it turns anything on. Apply on a Friday and you are waiting until Monday, so make this call before the truck arrives, not after. Its new service fee is $40, and deposits run $40 to $90 for owners and $60 to $140 for tenants depending on whether you need water, sewer, or both.
Inside city limits you deal with the city. Myrtle Beach bills water, sewer, sanitation, and stormwater on one monthly statement and sets the deposit by meter size. North Myrtle Beach charges a meter deposit, $180 for the common three-quarter-inch meter, plus a $50 service charge. Conway runs its own utility billing. On the Georgetown side, Pawleys Island and Litchfield are served by the Georgetown County Water and Sewer District.

### Gas, internet, and the rest
Natural gas is not everywhere. Dominion Energy is the gas utility, but the mains reach only some neighborhoods, so availability is checked address by address. Plenty of homes here are all electric or run propane, which matters if you were planning on a gas range.
For internet, HTC is a member-owned fiber cooperative covering much of the county, with published starting prices around $50 for 500 Mbps and about $75 for a gig. Spectrum is the incumbent cable provider and advertises lower first-year promotional rates that step up afterward. Brightspeed has fiber in parts of the city. Budget roughly $40 to $75 a month depending on the speed you need and whether you are still inside a first-year promotion.

The one nobody warns you about

## Outside the city limits, no truck comes for your trash
Inside the City of Myrtle Beach, trash is easy: about $34 a month on the same utility statement as water and sewer, which buys a garbage cart, a recycling cart, and two cubic yards of bulk and yard waste a week, all collected the same day. Carts go out no earlier than 6 p.m. the night before and come in by 11 p.m. on collection day, and that is a code the city actually enforces. Yard waste has to be in paper bags, not plastic.
In unincorporated Horry County there is no curbside collection at all. The county solid waste authority says so plainly, and nothing starts automatically when you close. You either haul your own to one of the 25 recycling and convenience centers, which are open to unincorporated residents only and cap you at four cubic yards a day, or you hire a private hauler, or your neighborhood association has a contract that covers it. Ask which of those three applies to the specific address before you close. People move here from cities and discover this on the second weekend.
One more line item: sales tax runs 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach and 8 percent everywhere else in Horry County. Unprepared groceries are taxed at zero either way.

Free beach parking

## The resident parking decal, and who actually qualifies
The City of Myrtle Beach gives residents a free parking decal that covers every city-owned paid space: the on-street meters and pay stations, the street-end beach accesses, the decal-only areas in The Avenues, and events at the convention center. It does not cover the Pavilion garage or any private lot. Given that beach access parking runs $3 an hour or $15 for the day in season, it is worth doing in your first month. Devin lived here more than a year before he learned the decal existed.
Fewer people qualify than assume they do. It is not for all Horry County residents. It is for vehicles that live inside the city limits and on which city vehicle property tax has been paid. The city treats that tax as your parking payment. If you live in Carolina Forest or Socastee or Surfside, you do not qualify, no matter how close you are.
Apply in person the first time, at the parking office in the Pavilion Parking Garage, 914 North Kings Highway, at the Ninth Avenue North entrance; the number is 843-626-7275 and hours are worth a call first. Renewals can be done online. Bring, for each vehicle, your South Carolina registration, your driver's license, and the current Horry County vehicle tax receipt, and note that the address on the license has to match the address on the tax receipt. Golf cart owners bring the state permit number too. The decal runs two years and replacements cost $20.
The other towns work differently and the details do not transfer. North Myrtle Beach has no physical decal at all; enforcement reads your license plate, registration renews every year, and its paid season runs March through October, 9 to 5. Myrtle Beach's paid season is shorter, March through September, but runs 9 a.m. to midnight. North Myrtle Beach does sell a limited number of annual passes to Horry County residents who live outside its limits, but the allocation is small and sells out early in the year, so it is not something to count on.

Getting around

## Golf cart rules, because this is a golf cart town
Many neighborhoods here run on golf carts, and the rules changed in 2025. To drive one on a public road you need a $5 state permit from the DMV, good for five years or until you move; proof of ownership and liability insurance; a driver who is at least 16 with a valid license; and the registration and insurance in the cart. Statewide, a permitted cart may run in daylight, on roads posted 35 mph or less, within four miles of the address on the permit (or of the gate, in a gated community), and may cross a faster road at an intersection. Every passenger under 12 must be belted.
Towns can add rules, and three of them have. North Myrtle Beach allows carts sunrise to sunset on 35 mph roads and lets them cross, but not drive along, Ocean Boulevard, 27th Avenue South, Highway 17, and Sea Mountain Highway; the fine is $100 and up to 30 days. Surfside Beach is the exception on hours: carts with permanently mounted headlights and taillights may run at night, carts without lights only from 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset. The City of Myrtle Beach keeps daylight hours, bars carts from sidewalks and multi-use paths, and closes Ocean Boulevard to carts over Memorial Day weekend. Outside city limits the state rules apply.
Before you buy in a neighborhood because it is “golf cart friendly,” check the posted speed limits on the roads between the house and wherever you plan to drive. A 45 mph road you cannot cross at an intersection ends the trip.

Once the license is done

## Register to vote, then look up your evacuation and flood zones
Voter registration closes 30 days before an election. You can register online at scvotes.gov once you have a South Carolina license or DMV ID, which is why it sits after the DMV step; the DMV license and golf cart forms also offer to pass your address to the election commission. Horry County's elections office is at 1515 Fourth Avenue in Conway. There is no residency waiting period and no party registration.
While you are on the county sites, look up two things for your new address: your hurricane evacuation zone on the state's Know Your Zone map, and the flood zone on FEMA's map service center. Both matter for insurance and both are on our coastal insurance page , along with what a wind and flood policy actually costs here.

Free, no obligation

Tell us where you are coming from and when. We will map your closing date against the 45-day registration window and the May 31 residence application deadline so you can see what falls due when. The filings are yours to make, and the county Auditor or a tax professional can confirm your own situation.

Common questions

## Moving to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### How long do I have to get a South Carolina driver's license after moving?
45 days. Third-party DMV sites still say 90, which is out of date. You go to a branch in person with proof of identity, your Social Security number, proof of your South Carolina address, and your old license, which you turn in. An eight-year license is $25 and there is a vision test.

### How much does it cost to register a car in South Carolina as a new resident?
About $305 per vehicle at the DMV: a one-time $250 infrastructure maintenance fee, a $15 title fee, and $40 for the plate and registration, which is good for two years. On top of that you pay the county's annual vehicle property tax before the DMV will issue the plate, and that amount depends on the vehicle's value.

### Why does the DMV send me to the county first?
Because South Carolina charges an annual property tax on vehicles, paid a year in advance, and the DMV will not register a car until it is paid. The county Auditor writes the tax notice, the Treasurer takes the payment, and the DMV needs the paid receipt. In Myrtle Beach the county office and the DMV branch face each other on 21st Avenue North, so it is one trip.

### What is the 4 percent legal residence application and when is it due?
It is the form that gets your primary home taxed at the owner-occupied rate instead of the second-home rate, which is roughly three times higher on the same house. Horry County asks for it by May 31 so your fall bill prints correctly. It requires a South Carolina driver's license and South Carolina vehicle registration for everyone on the deed, so do those first.

### Can I drive a golf cart on the road in Myrtle Beach?
Yes, with a $5 state permit that lasts five years, on roads posted 35 mph or less, within four miles of the address on the permit, in daylight unless the city has a night ordinance. Drivers must be 16 with a license and insurance, and children under 12 must be belted. North Myrtle Beach and Surfside Beach have their own rules on top of that.

### When can I register to vote in South Carolina?
As soon as you live here, and at least 30 days before any election you want to vote in. Online registration needs a South Carolina driver's license or DMV ID, so it comes after the license step. There is no waiting period and no party registration.

## Myrtle Beach Schools: Zones, Choice, and Registration
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/schools/
Summary: How to find the school an address is zoned for in Horry and Georgetown counties, why zones change, choice programs, and what to bring to register a child.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / Schools
Zones, choice programs, and registration

# Schools, for buyers moving to the Grand Strand.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer & licensed MLO, NMLS 2721275 · Reviewed by Timmy Fredrick Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated August 24, 2026
Two districts serve the Grand Strand. Zones are set by address, they change as schools are built, and the school names in a home's advertisement are not proof. Here is how to check an address yourself and who confirms it.
Ask about a specific address Call 854.333.2135

The direct answer

## How school zones work here
Horry County Schools serves all of Horry County: Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Conway, Carolina Forest, Socastee, Surfside Beach, Little River, Aynor, Loris, and the Horry side of Murrells Inlet. Georgetown County School District serves Pawleys Island, Litchfield, and the Georgetown side of Murrells Inlet. Every address is assigned one elementary, one middle, and one high school.
Horry County publishes an address lookup tool. Georgetown County does not, so you call the district. Both change zones when schools open or fill, so confirm the assignment for the exact address before you write an offer that depends on it.

How we handle this

## We do not rate schools, and here is why
Fair housing law prohibits steering, which means directing a buyer toward or away from an area based on a protected characteristic. Courts have treated an agent's opinions about schools as evidence of that, because phrases like “good schools” and “poor schools” can be used as code for who lives somewhere. So we do not rank schools, repeat ratings, or tell you which zone to want.
That is not a dodge. South Carolina publishes a report card for every public school, both districts publish their own data, and the people who can confirm a zone will answer the phone. Everything below is where that information lives and what to ask for. You reach your own conclusion, which is the only one that matters anyway.

Step one

## Check the exact address, not the neighborhood

### Horry County
The district runs an Attendance Zone Lookup that takes a street address and returns the assigned schools. The district's own instruction is to use it if you are new to the area and unsure, and to call the technology helpdesk at 843-488-6825 if questions remain. The tool is address-based, so a house under construction may not return a result until the lot has a posted address.
The district is organized into nine attendance areas: Aynor, Carolina Forest, Conway, Green Sea Floyds, Loris, Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Socastee, and St. James. It publishes a feeder chart showing which elementary schools lead to which middle and high schools, on its Our Schools page.

### Georgetown County
There is no public address lookup. Call the district office at 843-436-7000, or the school serving the area, and ask for the zoned school for that street address. Ask for it by email so you have it in writing. The district groups its schools into four areas, and the one covering Pawleys Island, Litchfield, and the Waccamaw Neck is the Waccamaw group.
One practical note for both districts: buses. Horry County does not transport students across attendance boundaries, and Georgetown County provides bus service to students living more than a mile and a half from their zoned school. If a child is close to a boundary, ask the district's transportation office what that means for your street before you commit.
This comes up in real transactions. One family moved here because their oldest child was starting at Coastal Carolina, and their younger child still needed a school. They knew which zone they wanted, and the houses they liked sat near its edge, some inside it and some not. We checked each address against the district lookup, told them which was which, and gave no opinion on any school. They picked with the full picture, and the younger child enrolled where the family intended. That is the service: not an opinion, a confirmed address.
Looking at a specific house? We will pull the zone with you and get it confirmed.
Ask about an address Call 854.333.2135

What to check

## Zones change, and this area is building schools
Horry County is one of the faster-growing counties in the country and the district builds to keep up. When two elementary schools opened in Carolina Forest, the board redrew the lines for three existing elementary schools and published the list of affected subdivisions by name. That process ran roughly four months from first draft to final vote, and the new lines took effect the following August. Another replacement school is in the district's capital plan.
Two things follow. First, the school names in a home's advertisement are not a district record. Agents and websites copy them forward for years without checking. Second, a zone you confirm in March can change for the school year after next. If a specific school assignment is the reason you are buying a particular house, confirm it with the district in writing, and understand you are confirming today's line.

### Capacity affects transfers, not enrollment
Each year Horry County publishes a list of schools at or above 95 percent of designed capacity, which the district calls Category 1 or Red Zone. A student zoned for one of those schools always enrolls there. What the designation does is close that school to elective transfers from outside its zone, with no exceptions for siblings or hardship. If your plan depends on transferring in, check the current list first. The list is republished every spring on the district's student transfer page.

The official data

## Read the state's report card yourself
South Carolina publishes an annual report card for every public school and district at screportcards.com . Each school's page carries an overall rating on a five-step scale, along with the underlying measures, and the site lets you compare schools and download the raw data files. It is a state publication, its methodology is public, and it is the source both districts point to.

1 Type the school's name in the Search for Your School box, or choose View Report Cards and browse by district.

2 The school's page shows the overall rating on the state's five-step scale, with the measures behind it: academics, student progress, graduation rate, college and career readiness, teacher qualifications, and the school climate surveys.

3 Use Compare Schools to put schools side by side, or open a district to see every school in Horry or Georgetown at once.

4 Report cards refresh each fall, so check the school year printed on the page before you rely on it.

We deliberately do not reprint any school's rating here, including the state's. Repeating a rating in our voice adopts it, and that is the line between giving you information and steering you. Look the schools up, decide what matters to you, and ask the district about anything the report card does not answer.
If you are not sure what to look at, the useful move is to decide first what you actually need. Class sizes, a specific special education service, a language, a music or arts program, a sport, distance from the house, bus eligibility, and start times are all things the district can answer directly and none of them are on a rating scale. Both districts list every school with contact numbers: Horry County and Georgetown County .

Beyond the zoned school

## Choice programs, transfers, and application windows

### Horry County optional secondary programs
The district runs a set of application-based programs that sit alongside the ten base high schools: the Academy for Arts, Science and Technology, the Academy for Technology and Academics, Scholars Academy, Early College High School, a Middle College at St. James, International Baccalaureate at three high schools, dual-credit programs with Horry-Georgetown Technical College, and technical scholars tracks in fields such as nursing, welding, and cybersecurity. Each publishes its own program guide and admission rubric.
Two mechanics matter to a family moving in. The application runs through the district's student portal in a short window in early May, so a mid-year arrival may be looking at the following year. And a student accepted into one of these programs is not classed as a transfer, which means transportation is provided; an ordinary elective transfer gets none. Program details and the application link are on the district's high school programs page.

### Transfers
Horry County accepts in-district transfer applications through June for the following year, approves them one year at a time, provides no transportation, and refuses transfers into schools at or above capacity. Students living in South Carolina but outside Horry County can apply to attend, with tuition set annually from the average per-pupil tax revenue; the figure for the most recent published year was $6,713, handled through the office of student affairs at 843-488-6770.
Georgetown County is different in kind, not degree. Its attendance zones were set under a 1970 federal court order and a later consent decree with the Department of Justice, and the district describes them as inflexible. Transfers are limited to the narrow categories written into district policy, and the application window closes in the spring. Ask the district rather than assuming.

### Georgetown County magnet programs
The district operates five magnet programs from kindergarten through twelfth grade, all in the Carvers Bay area in the western part of the county rather than on the Waccamaw Neck. Any student living in the district may apply, there is no cost, transportation is provided on request, and seats are assigned by a random computerized process among timely applications. The window has typically run in April; confirm the current year with the district.

Other options

## Charter, private, virtual, and home school
Charter schools are tuition-free public schools that operate outside a district's attendance zones, with their own applications and, when demand exceeds seats, a lottery. Several operate in Horry County and more have been approved, so the current roster is worth checking directly rather than trusting a list. South Carolina authorizes charters through statewide authorizers as well as districts; the state Department of Education keeps the charter schools program page with the accredited list.
Private schools are outside both districts and set their own admission timelines, which often close earlier in the year than public registration. South Carolina also runs a scholarship program that puts state funds in an account families can spend on approved education expenses. It has income limits, a participant cap, and a per-student cap, and its rules have changed more than once, so read the current terms on the state's school choice page before counting on it.
Home schooling is legal statewide under three different oversight options, and the state runs a free online public school program for full-time and supplemental courses. Both are described on the same state pages. We have no view on which of these is right for your family; we are listing them so the choice is visible.

Free, no obligation

We will pull the current attendance zone with you, point you at the district contact who confirms it in writing, and tell you what else that address means for cost. No opinions on schools, just the sources.

Enrolling

## What to bring, and the dates that bind
Horry County enrollment starts with an online pre-enrollment form for any student who was not in a district school at the end of the previous year. It asks you to upload four documents: a parent or guardian identification card, proof of residency, the student's birth certificate, and the student's immunization records. The school then emails you a code to finish the second stage. Registration for the coming year opens well before the school year starts.
Age cutoffs are firm: a child must be five years old by September 1 to enter kindergarten and six by September 1 for first grade. The four-year-old child development program has its own application, requires Horry County residence, adds a Medicaid card or proof of income to the document list, and assigns seats by priority points and a developmental screening rather than first come first served. Applications completed after mid-July go to a waiting list.
Georgetown County requires online registration for every student and asks for two forms of residency verification for a new student, plus the birth certificate and current immunization record. Returning students need one residency document.
Immunization is worth handling early. South Carolina requires a state certificate, and an out-of-state record usually has to be converted by a South Carolina provider or the health department before a school will accept it. That conversion takes an appointment, so it is a thing to start before the truck arrives rather than the week school opens.

If you have a college student

## In-state tuition takes twelve months
South Carolina charges in-state tuition to students whose family has been domiciled in the state for at least twelve continuous months before the first day of class, and the burden of proving it sits with the student. Moving in August does not make the fall semester in-state. There are exceptions, including one for people employed full time by a South Carolina employer, and each institution applies the state regulation itself. Coastal Carolina University and Horry-Georgetown Technical College both publish their residency pages, and the state Commission on Higher Education publishes the regulation. If a child is close to college age, ask the school's residency officer how your move date lands against their deadline.

Common questions

## Myrtle Beach schools FAQ

### How do I find out which school an address is zoned for in Horry County?
Use the district's Attendance Zone Lookup, which takes a street address and returns the assigned elementary, middle, and high school. If the address is new construction it may not return a result until the lot has a posted address. The district's helpdesk at 843-488-6825 answers zone questions, and the school's front office can confirm before you write an offer.

### Do school attendance zones change in Horry County?
Yes, and recently. When two elementary schools opened in Carolina Forest, the district moved the lines for three existing elementary schools and published the list of subdivisions that changed. The rezoning ran about four months from first draft to board vote, and the new lines took effect the following August. Never rely on the school names in a home's advertisement, and never assume this year's zone is next year's.

### Which school district serves Pawleys Island and Murrells Inlet?
It depends on the county line. Horry County Schools serves all of Horry County, which includes Myrtle Beach, North Myrtle Beach, Conway, Carolina Forest, Socastee, Surfside Beach, and the Horry side of Murrells Inlet. Georgetown County School District serves Pawleys Island, Litchfield, and the Georgetown side of Murrells Inlet.

### What documents do I need to register a child for school in Horry County?
Pre-enrollment is online and asks you to upload four things: a parent or guardian identification card, proof of residency, the student's birth certificate, and the student's immunization records. The school then sends a code to finish registration. A child must be five by September 1 for kindergarten and six by September 1 for first grade.

### Can my child attend a school we are not zoned for?
Sometimes. Horry County accepts in-district transfer applications through June, does not provide transportation for elective transfers, and denies transfers into schools at or above capacity. Its optional secondary programs are separate: students accepted there are not transfer students and do get transportation. Georgetown County's zones are set under a federal court order, so its transfers are limited to the narrow categories in district policy.

### Does Chapter3 Realty recommend schools?
No. Fair housing law treats an agent's opinions about schools as a form of steering, and we will not give you a different answer than we would give anyone else. South Carolina publishes a report card for every public school, and both districts publish their own data. This page points you to those sources and to the people who can confirm a zone.

## Moving From New York to Myrtle Beach: The Real Numbers
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-new-york/
Summary: What changes moving from New York to the Grand Strand: income and property tax, what your sale buys here, the yearly vehicle tax, and the residency trap.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / From New York
New York to the Grand Strand

# Moving from New York to Myrtle Beach.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer & licensed MLO, NMLS 2721275 · Reviewed by Timmy Fredrick Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated August 25, 2026
Most of the buyers we help are moving from New York. Here is what actually changes on paper, including the two costs that go up and the residency rule people miss.
Compare New York with here Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## What changes when you move
The table compares the two states for the 2026 tax year. Each line is explained below.

New York South Carolina

Top income tax rate 10.9%, nine brackets 5.21%, two brackets

Local income tax Yes in New York City and Yonkers None anywhere

Social Security Not taxed Not taxed

Government and military pensions Fully exempt, no cap Military exempt; other pensions taxed beyond the deductions

Property tax, statewide effective rate 1.30% 0.49%; Horry County about 0.38%

Median property tax bill $6,542 $1,337

Annual tax on your car None Yes, every year

Estate tax Yes, above about $7.35m None

Combined sales tax, typical About 8.5% 8% in Horry County, 9% in the city

Typical home value, July 2026 About $737,000 About $342,000

Rates are the 2026 tax year. Property figures are the most recent federal survey data. The calculator on our cost of living page runs the full comparison against your income.

Property tax

## Property tax depends on which part of New York you leave

### Long Island, Westchester and Rockland
The drop is large. Those counties carry effective property tax rates of roughly 1.6 percent in Suffolk, 1.7 percent in Nassau, 1.8 percent in Westchester and 2.1 percent in Rockland. Horry County runs about 0.38 percent on a primary home. The federal survey stops counting at $10,000, so the published medians for those counties are floors rather than actual figures. The real median bill in all four is above $10,000. On a comparable house here you are usually looking at a bill in the low thousands.
One client of ours left a house worth about $1 million and a property tax bill over $20,000 a year. They bought a similar sized house here for about $700,000, and the county bill on it runs about $3,200. Those are one household's rounded numbers, not a promise, but they show the scale of the gap.

### Brooklyn, Queens, Staten Island and the Bronx
The math is different in the boroughs. Effective rates run about 0.56 to 0.88 percent, because the city's assessment caps hold assessed values far below market value. That is already close to South Carolina's rates. You still gain on the purchase price. Do not expect a big drop in property tax.

### The 4 percent rate, and why you apply for it
South Carolina assesses a primary home at 4 percent of value and everything else at 6 percent. The 4 percent rate also removes the school operating tax, so the difference on the same house is roughly three to one. You have to apply for it. If you buy here before you sell in New York, or keep the New York house, this is the detail to get right. The property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.
Want the tax bill on a specific house, at your ownership status?
Run a real tax bill Call 854.333.2135

Pensions

## How South Carolina taxes a New York pension
New York does not tax New York State and local government pensions, federal pensions or military pensions. There is no dollar cap and no age test. If you retired from a New York school district, a police or fire department, a municipality or the state, New York taxes that pension at zero.
South Carolina treats it differently. Military retirement pay stays fully exempt at any age. A New York government pension is not military pay, so here it counts as ordinary retirement income. The shelter is smaller: a retirement income deduction of up to $3,000 a year before 65 and up to $10,000 from 65, plus a separate age-65 deduction of up to $15,000 against any income, reduced by whatever retirement deduction you already claimed.
For a large public pension, that can mean paying South Carolina tax on income New York was not taxing at all. The cheaper house and the lower property tax usually outweigh it, but not always. Run the numbers before you move, not after. Social Security is untaxed in both states.
Private pensions, 401(k)s and IRAs compare better. New York's exclusion for that income is capped at $20,000 per person from age 59 and a half, and withdrawals count against that cap. We are not tax advisers, and this is the point to bring one in. What we can do is tell you the housing side precisely.

Two costs that go up

## The car tax and the residency rule

### South Carolina taxes vehicles every year
New York charges a registration fee every two years and no property tax on cars. South Carolina charges a county property tax on every vehicle, every year, at 6 percent of the car's value, and the bill must be paid before your plate will renew. A $30,000 car runs roughly $360 a year outside the city limits and closer to $460 inside Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 county road fee. Arriving costs more still: a one-time $250 fee per vehicle, and you have 45 days from your move to register. A two-car household should plan on roughly $500 to $1,000 a year that did not exist in New York, and about $600 in one-time fees. The steps are on our new resident checklist , in order, because the county has to bill you before the DMV will issue a plate.

### New York can keep taxing you after you leave
This is the one that costs real money when it goes wrong. New York holds that your domicile does not change until you can show, in its words, with clear and convincing evidence that you abandoned it. There is a second test. Even after a genuine move, New York taxes you as a full-year resident if you keep a permanent home there for substantially all of the year and spend 184 days or more in the state.
Keep the Long Island house for the kids and spend half the year visiting, and you can end up filing and paying as a New York resident. If you plan to keep the northern property, or expect to spend much of the year back there, talk to a tax professional before you decide how the year will look. It also affects the 4 percent application here, which asks where you actually live.

Before you pick a neighborhood

## The mistake we see New York buyers make most
It is not a tax mistake. It is buying into a neighborhood whose rules do not fit how you plan to live. Most homes here sit inside an HOA, and the covenants decide real things: whether a boat or a trailer can park at the house, whether a golf cart can get you anywhere, whether you can rent the place out, and whether the pool and the social calendar you pictured actually exist there.
Buyers who skip the documents find out after closing. We read them with you before you offer. Start with our HOA guide and how to read HOA documents .

What the proceeds buy

## What your New York sale buys here
Overall prices here run about 17 percent below the New York metro area, and housing about 44 percent below. Utilities land about 31 percent lower, everyday goods about 13 percent lower, and other services about 7 percent lower. Typical rent is roughly $1,700 a month against about $3,600. The number most people care about is the house: about $342,000 typical here against about $737,000 there, in July 2026.
In practice that means a Nassau or Suffolk sale often clears a Grand Strand purchase outright, which is why so many buyers here pay cash, and why an offer backed by a strong pre-approval matters if you are financing. What you should not do is assume the whole difference is yours to keep. Insurance is higher, the car tax is new, and the first year is when people overspend. That trade is covered honestly on our pros and cons page .
The proceeds also buy differently town by town. Myrtle Beach on this page includes the towns around it: North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Murrells Inlet and Pawleys Island. The same budget buys a different house in each one, and seeing three towns in an afternoon is a normal showing day here, not a special request. The town by town page sets out how they differ.
One thing worth hearing from someone who deals with New York buyers weekly. People arriving from the Northeast tend to expect the pace and the directness they are used to, and it takes a season to adjust. Transactions here move differently, neighbors talk to you, and the summer is genuinely busy in a way winter is not. None of that shows up in a tax table, and all of it shapes whether the move sticks.

Common questions

## New York to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### How much cheaper is Myrtle Beach than New York?
Overall prices run about 17 percent lower than the New York metro area on the federal price index, and housing about 44 percent lower. In July 2026 the typical home was about $342,000 here against about $737,000 there. A household earning $95,000 in the New York metro keeps the same standard of living here on about $79,000.

### Will my property taxes go down if I move from New York to South Carolina?
From Long Island, Westchester or Rockland, substantially. Those counties run effective rates of roughly 1.6 to 2.1 percent, against about 0.38 percent in Horry County on a primary home. From Brooklyn, Queens or Staten Island, much less: the boroughs run about 0.56 to 0.88 percent because assessment caps hold assessed values well below market, so the gap is far smaller.

### Does South Carolina tax my pension if I move from New York?
Often, yes. New York fully exempts New York State and local government pensions, federal pensions and military pensions, with no cap. South Carolina exempts military retirement fully, but a state or municipal pension from New York becomes taxable here beyond the retirement and age-65 deductions. Social Security is untaxed in both states.

### Do I have to pay tax on my car every year in South Carolina?
Yes, and New York does not do this, so it surprises people. Vehicles are assessed at 6 percent of value at the full local rate, so a $30,000 car runs roughly $360 a year outside the city limits. You also pay a one-time $250 fee per vehicle when you first register it here, and you have 45 days from moving to do it.

### Can New York still tax me after I move to South Carolina?
It can, in two situations. New York says your domicile does not change until you can show with clear and convincing evidence that you abandoned it. Separately, even with a genuine domicile change, New York taxes you as a full-year resident if you keep a permanent home there for substantially all of the year and spend 184 days or more in the state. Keeping the old house and visiting family half the year is the common trap. Get advice from a tax professional before you plan your year.

### What is the biggest cost that goes up when moving from New York?
Insurance. A coastal policy here is often homeowners plus wind and hail plus flood, priced separately, with hurricane deductibles set as a percentage of the insured value. Get an insurance quote before you write an offer, because it changes the monthly number more than any other line.

## Moving From North Carolina to Myrtle Beach: The Close Call
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-north-carolina/
Summary: What changes moving from North Carolina to Myrtle Beach: the income tax crossover near $100,000, property and grocery taxes, gas, and what your sale buys here.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / From North Carolina
Carolina to Carolina

# Moving from North Carolina to Myrtle Beach.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer & licensed MLO, NMLS 2721275 · Reviewed by Timmy Fredrick Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated August 25, 2026
More people move to Myrtle Beach from North Carolina than from any other state. The tax gap is smaller than people assume, so here is the honest math, in both directions, and what actually changes at the coast.
Compare the Carolinas Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## North Carolina and South Carolina, side by side
The two states are closer on taxes than any other pair we compare. Each line is explained below.

North Carolina South Carolina

Income tax 3.99% flat 1.99% up to $30,000, then 5.21%

Local income tax None None

Social Security Not taxed Not taxed

Government pensions Some older state and federal pensions fully exempt Taxed past the retirement deductions; military fully exempt

Property tax, statewide effective rate 0.66% 0.49%; Horry County about 0.38% on a primary home

Median property tax bill $2,044 $1,337

Sales tax on groceries 2% 0% in Horry County

Annual tax on your car Yes Yes

Gas tax 41.25 cents a gallon 28.75 cents

Typical home value, July 2026 Charlotte about $389,000; Raleigh about $437,000 About $342,000

Rates are the 2026 tax year. Property figures are the most recent federal survey data. The calculator on our cost of living page runs the full comparison against your income.

What the sale buys

## What a Charlotte or Raleigh sale buys at the coast
A typical Charlotte home sells for about $389,000 and a typical Raleigh home about $437,000, against about $342,000 here. That is not the gap a New York seller sees, but it usually trades a suburban lot for a coastal one with money left over, and the property tax on it drops at the same time.
Myrtle Beach is the name people search, but the market around it is a set of towns: North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Murrells Inlet, Pawleys Island, Little River and inland Conway, each with its own prices. One of them may fit you better than the city itself, and we would love to show you the ones you have not seen on a weekend trip. What actually differs between them is laid out town by town .
Because the bills are this close, most North Carolina moves are about the coast itself, or a lifestyle change, not the tax math. The cost of living generally shifts less from North Carolina than from any other state we compare. The cost of living calculator shows whether your city runs more or less than Myrtle Beach and its surrounding areas, in about a minute.

Income tax

## The income tax can move either way, and the line sits near $100,000
North Carolina charges one flat rate on everything past its deduction. South Carolina charges a low rate on the first $30,000 and a higher one above it, with a deduction that shrinks as joint income climbs from $80,000 to $190,000.
We ran the two published schedules side by side for a married couple with no dependents. At $60,000 of income, South Carolina charges about $600 and North Carolina about $1,400. At $100,000 the two states land within a few dollars of each other. Above $100,000, South Carolina charges more, not less.
Dependents and credits move that line, so treat it as the shape of the comparison rather than your bill. What it means in practice: a working couple under $100,000 saves a little, a higher earner pays a little more, and nobody should make this move for the income tax alone.
Want the numbers on your own income and city?
Run my income comparison Call 854.333.2135

Pensions

## Check which kind of pension you hold before you move
North Carolina fully exempts some older government pensions: state, local and federal retirees who had five years of service before August 12, 1989, and military retirees with twenty years of service. If that is you, this move taxes income that has been tax free. South Carolina exempts military retirement fully at any age, but other government pensions are ordinary retirement income here, sheltered only by the deductions.
Every other retiree does better here. North Carolina taxes private pensions, 401(k)s and IRA withdrawals at the flat rate with no age break at all. South Carolina allows a retirement deduction of up to $3,000 before 65 and up to $10,000 from 65, plus a separate age-65 deduction of up to $15,000. Social Security is untaxed in both states.

The rest of the bill

## Groceries, gas, property tax and the car

### Groceries and gas get cheaper
North Carolina puts a 2 percent local tax on groceries. Horry County puts none. Gas runs about 12.5 cents a gallon cheaper here on the two states' published fuel taxes.

### Property tax drops, but modestly
Charlotte and Raleigh both run about 0.69 percent effective. Horry County runs about 0.38 percent on a primary home, and the primary rate also removes the school operating tax. It is a modest improvement, but it is still a few thousand dollars a year saved, usually on a bigger home. You apply for the primary rate yourself; the property tax page has the calculator and the deadline.

### The car tax is familiar
North Carolina already taxes vehicles every year with the registration, so this one is not a surprise. The mechanics differ: here the county bills you first and the plate renews after you pay, a car titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee at first registration, and you have 45 days from the move. The steps are on the new resident checklist .

### Sales tax goes up
General merchandise runs about 7.1 percent combined in North Carolina, against 8 percent in the county and 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach.

One recent move

## A North Carolina family who built here instead of buying
One of our recent North Carolina clients decided not to buy an existing house at all. They wanted out of North Carolina's taxes, a warmer coast, and a home built to their own plan, without ending up too far from family. We found the land, helped them vet a builder, and connected them with BrickWood Mortgage, which financed the construction.

Common questions

## North Carolina to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach cheaper than North Carolina?
Close, and it depends on the line. Houses cost less than Charlotte or Raleigh, groceries lose the 2 percent tax, gas is about 12 cents cheaper, and property tax is lower. Income tax is lower only below about $100,000 of joint income. The calculator on our cost of living page runs your exact city.

### Will my property taxes go down if I move from North Carolina to South Carolina?
Somewhat. Charlotte and Raleigh run about 0.69 percent effective while Horry County runs about 0.38 percent on a primary home, and the primary rate also removes the school operating tax. Expect a saving of a few thousand a year on a comparable house, not a windfall.

### Does South Carolina tax my North Carolina pension?
It depends which pension. Military retirement is exempt in both states. Some older North Carolina government pensions are fully exempt there and taxed here past the deductions, so that group should run the numbers first. Private pensions and 401(k)s usually do better here, because South Carolina has retirement deductions and North Carolina has none.

### Is the vehicle tax different in South Carolina?
The idea is the same: both states tax cars yearly with the plate. The mechanics differ here: the county bills you before the plate renews, a car titled elsewhere pays a one-time $250 fee, and you have 45 days from the move to register.

### How much do homes cost in Myrtle Beach compared with Charlotte or Raleigh?
A typical home here runs about $342,000, against about $389,000 in the Charlotte area and about $437,000 in the Raleigh area, on the same July 2026 measure.

### Why do so many people move from North Carolina to Myrtle Beach?
More people move to Myrtle Beach from North Carolina than from anywhere else. The usual reasons are the coast itself, more house for the money than the Charlotte or Raleigh metros, and retirement deductions North Carolina does not offer. The bills are close. The coast is the difference.

## Moving From Ohio to Myrtle Beach: What Actually Changes
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/from-ohio/
Summary: What changes moving from Ohio to Myrtle Beach: the city income taxes you leave, the vehicle tax you gain, the retiree math, and the Ohio residency rules.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / From Ohio
Ohio to the Grand Strand

# Moving from Ohio to Myrtle Beach.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer & licensed MLO, NMLS 2721275 · Reviewed by Timmy Fredrick Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated August 25, 2026
Devin, who wrote this page, made this exact move three years ago. Here is what changes on paper, what surprised him, and the one Ohio rule that follows you if you keep a foot in both states.
Get the Ohio comparison Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## Ohio and South Carolina, side by side
The state rates look close. The differences live in the local taxes, the car, and retirement income. Each line is explained below.

Ohio South Carolina

State income tax Flat 2.75% above $26,050 1.99% up to $30,000, then 5.21%

Local income tax City taxes, commonly 1% to 3%, and some school districts add their own None anywhere

Social Security Not taxed Not taxed

Pensions, 401(k)s and IRAs Taxed, with credits that top out at $200 a year Deductions up to $10,000 from 65, plus an age-65 deduction

Property tax, statewide effective rate 1.36% 0.49%; Horry County about 0.38% on a primary home

Median property tax bill $2,937 $1,337

Annual tax on your car No Yes, every year

Gas tax 38.5 cents a gallon 28.75 cents

Typical home value, July 2026 Cleveland area about $254,000 About $342,000

Rates are the 2026 tax year. Property figures are the most recent federal survey data. The calculator on our cost of living page runs the full comparison against your income.

Income tax

## The tax that disappears is the local one
Ohio's state rate is one of the lowest in the country. What most Ohio households actually feel is the layer under it: city income taxes, commonly 1 to 3 percent of wages, and in some places a school district income tax on top of that.
South Carolina has no local income tax anywhere. No city rate, no district rate. For a working household this is the largest single income-tax change in the whole comparison, and it is bigger than the difference between the two state rates.

Retirees

## Retirement income: the clearest win of any state we compare
Ohio taxes pensions, 401(k) and IRA withdrawals at its flat rate. The relief is a retirement credit that tops out at $200 a year, one per return, and disappears entirely at $100,000 of income, plus a $50 credit at 65.
South Carolina works from deductions instead: up to $3,000 of retirement income before 65 and up to $10,000 from 65, per person, plus a separate age-65 deduction of up to $15,000 against any income. Social Security is untaxed in both states. For most retirees the same pension is simply taxed less here, and the property tax on the house drops at the same time.
Retiring here from Ohio? We will run your whole picture.
Run my retirement math Call 854.333.2135

The other direction

## Two things cost more here, and Devin hit both

### South Carolina taxes your car every year
Ohio charges a flat registration of roughly $36 plus small local fees, and nothing based on the car's value. Here every vehicle is taxed yearly on its value: a $30,000 car runs roughly $360 outside the city limits and closer to $460 inside Myrtle Beach, plus a $50 road fee, and the county bill must be paid before the plate renews. Arriving adds a one-time $250 fee per vehicle, with 45 days to register. A two-car household should plan on roughly $500 to $1,000 a year that did not exist in Ohio. The bill for boats and campers works the same way. Devin, who wrote this page, arrived from Ohio three years ago, and this tax was the item that caught him: his first county bill was $325 for the car, plus the one-time $250 fee and the $50 road fee. The steps, in order, are on the new resident checklist .

### Houses and sales tax
A typical home here costs about $342,000 against about $254,000 in the Cleveland area, so the purchase itself is a step up for many Ohio buyers even though the tax rate on it is far lower. The figure is the Myrtle Beach metro; the towns around it price differently. If you are coming from a small town, you do not have to land in a resort city: Conway, Longs, Aynor and Little River all sit within a short drive of the beach, and we are glad to show them next to the beachfront so you can compare. The which town page compares all of them properly. Sales tax runs 8 percent in the county and 9 percent in the city, against about 7.3 percent combined in Ohio. Groceries are untaxed in both.

If you keep a foot in Ohio

## Ohio has a residency test with real teeth
Ohio presumes you are still a resident until you show otherwise, and its test is specific. You cannot hold an Ohio driver's license at any point in a year you claim to be gone. Your days back in Ohio are counted, and at 213 or more the presumption becomes very hard to beat. And the non-residency statement has a hard deadline: filed by October 15 of the following year, it makes your non-resident status final; missed, Ohio presumes you never left.
If the plan is a clean move, surrender the license early and the rest follows. If the plan is a winter here and a summer there, bring in a CPA before you set up the year, not after.

First hand

## What surprised Devin after the move
Devin moved here from Pleasant City, a village of about 400 people in Guernsey County, Ohio. Three years in, three things stand out to him. The county vehicle bill, which Ohio never sends; the numbers are further up this page. Needing sunglasses: he never owned a pair that mattered in Ohio and reaches for them daily here in summer. Common questions

## Ohio to Myrtle Beach FAQ

### Is Myrtle Beach cheaper than Ohio?
Mostly, not entirely. Local income tax disappears, gas runs about 10 cents cheaper, and property tax rates are far lower. Against that, a typical house costs more than the Cleveland area, sales tax is higher, and the yearly car tax is new. The calculator on our cost of living page runs your exact city.

### Do I pay local income tax in Myrtle Beach?
No. South Carolina has no city or school district income tax anywhere. Most Ohio cities charge 1 to 3 percent of wages, so for working households this is usually the biggest single change.

### How is retirement income taxed in South Carolina compared with Ohio?
Ohio taxes pensions and retirement account withdrawals with credits that top out at $200 a year. South Carolina allows deductions instead: up to $10,000 of retirement income from age 65 per person, plus an age-65 deduction of up to $15,000. Social Security is untaxed in both.

### Does South Carolina really tax my car every year?
Yes. Vehicles are taxed yearly on value: a $30,000 car runs roughly $360 to $460 plus a $50 road fee, and the bill must be paid before the plate renews. Ohio charges a flat fee of roughly $36 to $74. Add a one-time $250 fee per vehicle when you arrive, within 45 days.

### Can Ohio still tax me after I move to South Carolina?
It can if the move is not clean. Holding an Ohio driver's license at any point in the year, spending 213 or more day-pairs back in Ohio, or missing the October 15 non-residency statement each keep Ohio's claim alive. A snowbird split between the two states should bring in a CPA first.

### What surprised Devin most after moving from Ohio?
The county vehicle bill, which Ohio never sends: every vehicle here is taxed on its value each year. Then two he did not see coming: needing sunglasses daily in summer, and a job market far wider than Pleasant City, the village of about 400 he left.

## Which Grand Strand Town Is Right for You?
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/which-town/
Summary: Conway to Pawleys Island, what actually differs between Grand Strand towns: price ranges, city versus county rules, short-term rental limits and real drive times.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / Which Town
Town by town

# Which Grand Strand town is right for you.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer & licensed MLO, NMLS 2721275 · Reviewed by Timmy Fredrick Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated August 25, 2026
Myrtle Beach is one name for a run of towns with different prices and different rules. Four things actually differ, and all four are a matter of record.
Shortlist my towns Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## What actually differs between them
People search Myrtle Beach and then buy somewhere else on this list, because the name covers about sixty miles of coast plus the inland towns behind it. The differences that change a purchase are these four, in this order.
Whether the address is inside a city or town, or in unincorporated county. That one line decides your sales tax, your trash collection, your beach parking decal, and who writes the zoning, golf cart and rental rules that apply to you.
What your budget reaches. The starting price in Conway and the starting price on Pawleys Island are more than $300,000 apart.
Whether you can rent it out. This varies more between towns here than anything else, and an HOA can forbid what the zoning allows.
The drive. To work, to a hospital, to the airport. Everything is closer than it looks on a map, until July.

Side by side

## The towns, with prices and rules

Area Price range Governed by Short-term rentals

Little River $150,000 to $800,000 Unincorporated county Generally allowed under county rules

North Myrtle Beach $300,000 to $2,500,000+ City Annual permit, business license and a responsible party

Myrtle Beach $150,000 to $1,500,000+ City Limited zones only; most residential zones no

Carolina Forest Mostly newer construction Unincorporated county County rules, but HOA covenants usually decide

Conway $120,000 to $500,000 City Allowed under city and county rules

Surfside Beach $250,000 to $1,500,000 Town Certain zones only

Garden City $225,000 to $1,200,000 Mostly unincorporated county Generally allowed under county rules

Murrells Inlet $200,000 to $1,000,000+ Unincorporated county Allowed; rules differ by county line and by HOA

Pawleys Island $450,000 to $5,000,000+ Town, plus unincorporated mainland Generally allowed, subject to zoning and HOA

Price ranges are the working ranges on each area page and move with the market. Rental rules are summarized; the governing document for any address is the municipal ordinance and the HOA covenants, not this table. Murrells Inlet and Pawleys Island straddle the Horry and Georgetown county line, which changes which county rules apply.

Not sure which of these your budget reaches?
Shortlist my towns Call 854.333.2135

City or county

## The line that changes four bills at once
This is the difference people miss, because it does not show up in a listing. Whether an address sits inside a municipality or in unincorporated Horry County changes all of the following.

### Sales tax
Nine percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach, eight percent in the county. Groceries are untaxed either way.

### Trash
Curbside collection is a city service. Outside city limits you arrange it yourself, and the options and costs are on the new resident checklist .

### Beach parking
The free resident parking decal is issued by the city to city residents. Living two streets outside the line means paying at the meters.

### Golf carts and rentals
Both are set by whoever governs the address. A golf cart that is legal on your street may not be legal a mile away, and short-term rental rules change at the same line. Check the address, not the town name.

The drive

## Everything is closer than it looks, until July
Off-peak driving times to Myrtle Beach, measured on the road network with no traffic in them: Surfside Beach about 15 minutes over 8 miles, Carolina Forest about 20 minutes over 10 miles, Conway about 25 minutes over 14 miles, Murrells Inlet about 25 minutes over 17 miles, North Myrtle Beach about 30 minutes over 20 miles, Pawleys Island about 35 minutes over 26 miles.
Those are a model, not a promise. US-17 in July is a different road, and the local workaround is to use SC-31 or SC-22 rather than the highway with all the traffic lights on it.
Two drives are worth measuring before you choose an area rather than after: the one to whatever medical care your household actually depends on, which the healthcare page sets out, and the one to work if you will be earning here, which the jobs page covers.

How we do this

## We give you the records, not our opinion of a neighborhood
Fair housing law is strict about agents steering buyers toward or away from areas, and it is strict for good reason. So we do not describe who lives in an area, and you should be wary of any agent who does.
What we do instead is hand over what is written down. Zoning and short-term rental rules are municipal ordinances. Rental caps and minimum lease terms are in the HOA covenants. Flood zones are on the federal maps. School attendance zones are on the state and district lookup tools, which the schools page shows you how to use. Every one of those is a document you can read yourself, and we will get you all of them for any address before you make an offer.
Tell us what the house has to do and what it has to be near. That is a question about property, and it is one we can answer properly.

Common questions

## Grand Strand towns FAQ

### What towns make up the Grand Strand?
Running north to south: Little River, North Myrtle Beach, Myrtle Beach itself, Carolina Forest and Socastee inland, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Murrells Inlet and Pawleys Island, with Conway inland on the Waccamaw River. Some are incorporated cities and towns and some are unincorporated county, which changes the rules that apply.

### Which Grand Strand town is the cheapest?
On the price ranges we publish for each area, Conway starts lowest at about $120,000 and Little River at about $150,000. Pawleys Island starts highest at about $450,000. Every area has a wide range, so the starting figure matters less than what your budget reaches in each one.

### Does it matter if a house is inside city limits?
Yes, in four practical ways. Sales tax is 9 percent inside the City of Myrtle Beach against 8 percent in the county. Curbside trash collection is a city service, so outside city limits you arrange it yourself. The free resident beach parking decal is for city residents. And zoning, golf cart and short-term rental rules are set by whoever governs that address.

### Can I rent out a house on the Grand Strand?
It depends entirely on the address. Myrtle Beach allows short-term rentals only in limited zones. North Myrtle Beach requires an annual permit, a business license and a responsible party. Surfside Beach allows them in certain zones only. Unincorporated county areas are generally more permissive. An HOA can also forbid what the zoning allows.

### How far apart are the Grand Strand towns?
Closer than people expect. Off-peak from Myrtle Beach it is about 15 minutes to Surfside Beach, 20 to Carolina Forest, 25 to Conway and to Murrells Inlet, 30 to North Myrtle Beach and 35 to Pawleys Island. Summer traffic on US-17 makes all of those longer, sometimes much longer.

### How do you decide which town to show me?
By what you tell us the house has to do: your budget, what it needs to be near, whether you intend to rent it, and whether you want a golf cart to be legal on your roads. We work from published records, zoning, covenants and permits, and we give you the documents to read yourself rather than characterizing who lives in an area.

## Jobs in Myrtle Beach, SC: What the Economy Actually Pays
URL: https://chapter3realty.com/buyers/relocating/jobs/
Summary: What work exists in Myrtle Beach, who the largest employers are, what the average job pays against the national average, and how seasonal the year really is.

Home / Buyers / Relocating / Jobs and the Economy
Work on the Grand Strand

# Jobs and the economy in Myrtle Beach.
By Devin Day , Operations Officer & licensed MLO, NMLS 2721275 · Reviewed by Timmy Fredrick Nash , Broker-in-Charge · Updated August 25, 2026
The pay here is lower than most places people move from. This page gives you the real numbers, who does the hiring, and how much the year swings.
Talk through my move Call 854.333.2135

The short answer

## What the local economy is built on
Horry County had 146,055 covered jobs across 12,762 workplaces in 2025. The county and the metro area are now the same thing: Brunswick County, North Carolina moved into the Wilmington metro in 2023, so every county figure on this page is also the metro figure.
One job in four is in leisure and hospitality, and that is the whole story behind the wage numbers further down. There is no dominant factory and no corporate headquarters here. The largest employer is the school district.

Industry Jobs here Share of jobs Average week US average week

Leisure and hospitality 36,321 24.9% $566 $657

Trade, transport and utilities 32,162 22.0% $795 $1,241

Education and health services 16,909 11.6% $1,244 $1,278

Professional and business services 13,640 9.3% $1,177 $2,086

Construction 9,598 6.6% $1,273 $1,631

Financial activities 7,605 5.2% $1,326 $2,556

Manufacturing 3,372 2.3% $1,157 $1,721

Information 1,644 1.1% $1,589 $3,671

Private-sector jobs and average weekly wages, annual 2025, from the federal employment and wage survey. The share column is our arithmetic against the 146,055 all-ownership total.

The number that matters

## The average job here paid $50,053 in 2025
The national figure for the same year was $78,722. That is about 64 cents on the national dollar, and we are not going to dress it up. Two thirds of the gap is the industry mix in the table above: manufacturing is 2.3 percent of jobs here against 8.1 percent nationally, and leisure and hospitality is more than twice the national share.
Households do better than that number suggests, because it counts jobs rather than people. Median household income in the county is $66,880, against $69,324 for South Carolina and $80,734 nationally. A two-earner household is described by that second figure, not the first.
What this means when you are looking at a house: your lender qualifies you on your income, not on the local average. If you keep a remote job at northern pay, this page is not about you. If you are going to earn here, work the numbers on a house from a local salary before you fall for a listing price, and the cost of living calculator will show you what your current income is worth here.
Want to know what a local salary buys here?
Run my income both ways Call 854.333.2135

Who hires

## The largest employers are schools, hospitals, shops and government
This is the county's own audited list, as of June 2025. The ten together employ 22,658 people, about 12.3 percent of everyone working here.

Employer Employees

Horry County School District 6,643

Wal-Mart and Sam's Club 2,813

Horry County Government 2,652

Conway Medical Center 2,035

McLeod Health, Loris and Seacoast 1,777

Food Lion 1,659

Grand Strand Regional Medical Center 1,655

Coastal Carolina University 1,541

City of Myrtle Beach 1,269

Horry Telephone Company 614

Two things follow from that list. If you work in health care, education or the trades, the hiring here is steady and the wage gap against the rest of the country is at its narrowest: education and health services pay $1,244 a week here against $1,278 nationally. If you are a senior manager in a corporate function, there are very few chairs, because there is no headquarters to sit in.
There is manufacturing, but not much of it. The regional development corporation lists Kyocera AVX as the largest industrial employer at about 1,000 people, then Apollo Valves, Canfor Southern Pine, Pepsi Bottling Ventures and Metglas. Health care is the sector adding capacity fastest, because three hospitals are being built at once, which is covered on the healthcare page .

The season

## Unemployment swings 2.8 points between winter and spring
Because a quarter of the jobs follow the tourist season, unemployment here swings on a schedule. In January 2026 the county rate was 7.0 percent. In April 2026 it was 4.2 percent. In June 2026 it was 4.7 percent, still preliminary. Those are the same county in the same year.
The shape repeats: the rate peaks in January and February, bottoms out in April, and rises again in late summer. Anyone quoting you one month without saying which month is telling you very little.
Who this actually changes things for: hourly workers in hospitality, and anyone self-employed in a trade that serves visitors. Both should look at a full year of income rather than a good month before deciding what house payment they are comfortable with. Salaried work in the hospitals, the schools and the county does not move with the season at all.
