## Real estate investing in Murrells Inlet, SC
Murrells Inlet is the Seafood Capital of South Carolina, and its identity is built around the water rather than the beach. The MarshWalk, a half-mile boardwalk of waterfront restaurants and live music, anchors a community of creek-front homes, golf communities, and established single-family neighborhoods. There is no wide public beach in the inlet itself; beach access comes via neighboring Garden City, which shapes how the rental market behaves.
That distinction makes Murrells Inlet more of a primary-residence and long-term-rental market than a pure vacation-rental corridor. Investors here are often buying for steady cash flow and appreciation rather than peak-summer nightly rates, and the buyer pool leans toward primary residents and second-home owners drawn to the golf and the waterfront lifestyle.

## Murrells Inlet property types and pricing
The inventory leans single-family: golf-community homes around Wachesaw Plantation and TPC Myrtle Beach, creek-front and marsh-view properties with docks, and conventional neighborhoods set back from the water. Condos exist but are less central than in the beach towns. Waterfront and golf-community homes command premiums; inland single-family offers more approachable entry for a long-term-rental strategy.
Dock access and deep-water frontage are the features that carry the most value here, drawing boaters and a specific lifestyle buyer that inland inventory cannot reach.

## Where investors are looking in Murrells Inlet
Investor and primary-residence demand clusters around the golf and waterfront communities. Wachesaw Plantation and the TPC Myrtle Beach area anchor the premium golf-community market. Prince Creek is the large master-planned choice with a range of price points. Creek-front homes near the MarshWalk carry the highest waterfront premiums, while Blackmoor and the inland subdivisions offer more approachable single-family entry for a long-term-rental strategy.

## The Murrells Inlet rental market
Long-term rental is the steadier play in Murrells Inlet, supported by the year-round population and proximity to jobs across the southern Strand. Short-term rental exists, particularly for waterfront and golf properties marketed to visitors who want the inlet experience, but it is more limited and more rules-dependent than the beachfront markets. The result is a market that rewards buy-and-hold investors who value stability over seasonal upside.

## How rental returns work in Murrells Inlet
Long-term-rental math governs most of Murrells Inlet. Start with achievable monthly rent, subtract the 35 to 45 percent that taxes, insurance, maintenance, HOA dues, and management typically take, and judge the deal on cash flow and cash-on-cash return. Golf-community homes carry higher dues that compress yield, so factor them honestly. The appeal here is predictability: year-round demand means fewer vacancy surprises than a seasonal beach asset.

## Financing an investment property in Murrells Inlet
Because the strategy here leans long-term, financing is comparatively clean. Conventional investment loans and DSCR loans that qualify on rent both fit single-family rentals well. Golf-community homes are standard collateral, though lenders will note the HOA dues in the debt-to-income or coverage math. Primary-residence buyers, common in this market, get the best terms of all.

## Murrells Inlet rules and costs that move the numbers
The tax treatment matters here because so many buyers are choosing between primary residence and investment. South Carolina assesses a primary residence at 4 percent and non-owner-occupied property at 6 percent, a meaningful gap that changes the yield on a rental. Golf-community homes add HOA dues on top. If a property fronts the creek or marsh, factor flood insurance as well. Confirm the current millage, ratio, and dues for the specific home before you treat any quoted return as real.

## The Murrells Inlet investor thesis

- 01 Long-term rental cash flow and appreciation are the core thesis, supported by a real year-round population.

- 02 Golf-community and creek-front homes with docks are premium, defensible assets with a dedicated buyer pool.

- 03 The year-round and second-home base provides demand that does not depend on the summer tourist calendar.

- 04 Short-term rental is a selective add-on for waterfront and golf properties, not the default strategy.

## What a first Murrells Inlet deal looks like
A typical first deal here is a single-family home held as a long-term rental, often in an established neighborhood rather than a golf community where dues compress yield. Start with an achievable monthly rent, subtract a realistic expense load, and confirm the cash-on-cash return works on conservative numbers. Because demand is year-round rather than seasonal, a Murrells Inlet first deal is usually about steady, unglamorous cash flow, which for a first investment is a feature rather than a flaw.

## What to watch before you buy in Murrells Inlet

- Beach access reality. The inlet has no wide public beach. Price short-term-rental expectations accordingly; this is not Garden City.

- HOA and golf-community fees. Premium communities carry dues that affect net yield. Factor them in.

- Dock permitting and condition. Waterfront value hinges on the dock. Confirm permits and structural condition before you pay the premium. Dock permits, build costs, and flood zones are covered in our waterfront homes guide .

## Where Murrells Inlet is, and why the county line matters
Murrells Inlet sits about 13 miles, a 20 to 25 minute drive, south of Myrtle Beach along U.S. 17, and it is unincorporated, which means the county governs it directly rather than a town council. The community straddles two counties: the northern portion falls in Horry County and the southern portion in Georgetown County. That one fact drives three things buyers care about here, because short-term-rental rules, school assignment, and county millage all change depending on which side of the line an address sits on.
It is a car-dependent area. Roughly nine in ten households own at least one vehicle and public transit is limited, so plan on driving to the beach, the airport, and daily errands. Myrtle Beach International Airport is about 20 to 25 minutes north.

## The Murrells Inlet market right now
Murrells Inlet is a buyer's market as of mid-2026, with homes taking well longer than the national norm to sell. Public trackers put the median sale price in a wide band, from the mid $330,000s to about $445,000 depending on the source, month, and whether condos are included, with median days on market reported between roughly 90 and 175. Redfin reported a median near $360,000 in early 2026. Those aggregator figures disagree because each uses a different geography and date range, so treat them as a range, not a single truth.
For an accurate, current figure we pull directly from the Coastal Carolinas MLS for the exact area and property type you are considering, which is what actually reflects closings. The strongest window to list here is generally February through July, when buyer demand peaks.

## What it costs to own in Murrells Inlet: the 4 percent versus 6 percent property tax rule
Your South Carolina property-tax bill depends on how you use the home, not just its value. A primary, owner-occupied residence is assessed at a 4 percent ratio and qualifies for the owner-occupant school-operating credit. A second home or investment property is assessed at 6 percent and does not get that credit, so the effective tax on the same house can run close to double when it is not your primary residence. See the South Carolina Department of Revenue for the assessment-ratio rules. Millage also differs between the Horry and Georgetown County portions of Murrells Inlet, one more reason the county line matters. Full county math, with a calculator: Horry County property taxes .

## Short-term rental rules in Murrells Inlet
Short-term rentals are allowed in Murrells Inlet, but the rules depend on the county and the HOA, not on the community name alone. On the Georgetown County side, the county treats a rental of under 30 days as a residential use and does not require a special short-term-rental permit in most zones, though owners still need a county business license and must collect and remit accommodations tax. See Georgetown County zoning for specifics. On the Horry County side, the property follows Horry County's unincorporated rules, which are more restrictive in some residential zones. In both counties an HOA or planned-unit development can restrict or ban short-term rentals regardless of what the county allows, and enforcement is generally complaint-driven. Chapter3 will verify the zoning for the exact address and pull the HOA governing documents before you assume a property can be rented nightly. Every jurisdiction's licenses and taxes: short-term rental rules by city .

## Flood zones and insurance in Murrells Inlet
Flood risk is a real cost factor here because the community is built around a saltwater estuary and tidal creeks. Homes inside a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area generally require flood insurance when financed with a federally backed loan, and First Street data reported by Redfin flags a meaningful share of Murrells Inlet properties as having severe flood risk over a 30-year horizon. Pull the FEMA flood map, and on waterfront or low-lying lots an elevation certificate, for the specific address, since the zone and the premium can change block to block. What the three coastal policies cost: coastal home insurance costs .

## Murrells Inlet lifestyle and amenities
The center of gravity in Murrells Inlet is the water, not a wide beach. The half-mile MarshWalk boardwalk anchors the dining and live-music scene along the estuary, and two working marinas, Crazy Sister Marina and Marlin Quay Marina, put boating, fishing charters, and the inlet within reach. Just south, Brookgreen Gardens, a National Historic Landmark with the country's largest collection of American figurative sculpture and a Lowcountry zoo, and Huntington Beach State Park give the area a nature-and-culture draw most of the Grand Strand lacks. Golf is deep, with courses including TPC Myrtle Beach, Wachesaw Plantation, and Blackmoor nearby. Everyday needs are covered by Publix, The Fresh Market, and Lowes Foods, and Tidelands Waccamaw Community Hospital serves the area. Wide public beach access is a short drive north in Garden City.

## Schools serving Murrells Inlet
School assignment in Murrells Inlet depends on the county side and the exact address. Properties on the Horry County side are generally served by the St. James attendance area within Horry County Schools , including St. James Elementary, St. James Intermediate, St. James Middle, and St. James High on Highway 707, with Seaside Elementary serving parts of the area. Properties on the Georgetown County side are generally served by the Waccamaw schools within the Georgetown County School District. Because the two districts meet inside Murrells Inlet, Chapter3 will confirm the exact assignment for any address against the district attendance-boundary map.

## What is coming in Murrells Inlet
Murrells Inlet already connects to the rest of the Grand Strand through the Carolina Bays Parkway, S.C. 31, which currently terminates at S.C. 707 at the edge of the community. The larger S.C. 31 extension that appears in regional news runs northward toward the North Carolina line, a future Interstate 74 corridor funded on the South Carolina side through Horry County's RIDE III program with S.C. construction targeted around 2029 per SCDOT statements reported locally , so it matters more to the North Strand than to the inlet directly.

## What it is like to live in Murrells Inlet
For a primary or second home, Murrells Inlet is built around the water rather than a wide beach. Daily life centers on the half-mile MarshWalk, two working marinas, and the estuary, with Brookgreen Gardens and Huntington Beach State Park just south for nature and culture most of the Strand lacks. It is quieter and more residential than the Myrtle Beach core, and wide public beach access is a short drive north in Garden City.
Everyday needs are covered by Publix, The Fresh Market, and Lowes Foods, and Tidelands Waccamaw Community Hospital serves the area. As a live-in buyer, the numbers that shape daily life here are the flood elevation and insurance cost for the exact lot, the regime or HOA dues on a condo, and the community rules, more than nightly-rate projections.

## Buying in Murrells Inlet to live, not just to rent
Much of what is written about Murrells Inlet is aimed at investors, but many buyers here want a full-time residence or a second home on the water. If you are buying to live, weigh boat and dock access, the walk or drive to the MarshWalk, and how seasonal your specific street gets. The primary-versus-second-home choice also changes your tax bill: a primary residence is assessed at 4% with the owner-occupant credit, a second home at 6% without it, so budget for the higher effective rate if this will not be your full-time home.

## Read the Murrells Inlet HOA rules before you commit to a house
In a market with this many associations, the covenants matter as much as the house. Before you make an offer, read the HOA bylaws and rules, because they can restrict short-term and long-term rentals, pets, parking, golf carts, fences, and exterior changes. The classic trap: you have spent years training your dog to walk off leash, then buy into a community with a strict leash rule and lose the thing you valued most. Read the documents before you make an offer, not after.
Ask us and we will get you the governing documents for any Murrells Inlet community, from our own files if we already have them or by requesting them for you if we do not. It is also why a Chapter3 agent asks a lot of questions about how you actually live: we would rather spend the time up front than match you to a home with a rule or an HOA that blocks what you enjoy or turns out to be a poor investment.

## Who Murrells Inlet suits
Murrells Inlet fits buyers who want a waterfront and golf lifestyle over beachfront nightlife, and it rewards a specific kind of investor. Because wide beach access is a drive away in Garden City, the numbers here favor long-term and mid-term rentals and steady appreciation more than pure peak-summer nightly rates, the opposite of an oceanfront-condo play. Primary-residence buyers, second-home owners, and buyers targeting a specific gated or golf community also do well here. If your plan depends on high-season nightly rental income, an oceanfront submarket like Garden City or Myrtle Beach usually pencils better, and we will tell you that rather than sell you the wrong street.

Both. Murrells Inlet is unincorporated and straddles Horry County to the north and Georgetown County to the south, which changes short-term-rental rules, school assignment, and county taxes depending on the address.

### What are property taxes like on a second home in Murrells Inlet?
Higher than on a primary residence. Not a wide public beach of its own. Murrells Inlet is built around a saltwater estuary and the MarshWalk, and the nearest wide public beach access is a short drive north in Garden City.

# Myrtle Beach, SC Real Estate Market

## The Myrtle Beach, SC housing market
Myrtle Beach is the center of gravity for the entire Grand Strand. The city holds the densest concentration of rentable oceanfront units on the coast, draws the bulk of the region's roughly 19 million annual visitors, and trades more inventory more often than any other submarket here. For an investor, that liquidity matters: it is easier to buy, easier to sell, and easier to find comparable sales and rental history than anywhere else on the Strand.
The market splits cleanly into two worlds. Along Ocean Boulevard, the Boardwalk corridor, and Kings Highway, the inventory is overwhelmingly resort condominiums built and operated for short-term vacation rental. Move a few miles inland to Carolina Forest, The Market Common, or Socastee, and you find conventional single-family neighborhoods that behave like a normal residential market with long-term tenants and owner-occupants.

## Myrtle Beach property types and pricing
The entry point for most first-time investors is an oceanfront studio or one-bedroom condo inside an established rental program. These are the most liquid, most financeable, and most predictable units in the market. Two-bedroom oceanfront and resort condos step up in both price and revenue. Inland, single-family homes and townhomes serve the long-term rental and primary-residence buyer.
Pricing spans a wide band, from sub-$200,000 oceanfront studios to single-family and luxury oceanfront well past seven figures. Because the spread is so wide, the median list price and median nightly rate vary enormously by building and corridor. For current figures on a specific building or street, a licensed agent can pull live CCAR MLS and rental data. Weighing a condo purchase? Read our guide: Are Myrtle Beach condos a good investment?

## Where investors are looking in Myrtle Beach
Within the city, investor demand concentrates in a few distinct pockets. The Ocean Boulevard high-rise corridor is the heart of the short-term-rental market, with the deepest pool of rentable condos and rental-program history. The Golden Mile holds single-family oceanfront for higher-budget buyers. The Shore Drive and Arcadian Shores area north of the strip mixes condos with strong rental demand and a slightly quieter setting. For long-term-rental and primary-residence plays, Carolina Forest is the dominant inland choice, with The Market Common offering a walkable, newer-construction alternative and Socastee providing the most approachable single-family entry.

## The Myrtle Beach rental market
Short-term rental is the dominant strategy near the ocean, and revenue follows a sharp seasonal curve. Summer weeks command premium nightly rates and near-full occupancy, shoulder seasons soften, and winter thins out everywhere except the snowbird-friendly buildings. The single biggest driver of return is not the unit's finish level but the building's rental program and location: the right building can produce forty percent more revenue than a nearly identical unit a block away.
Short-term rental eligibility is not uniform. The City of Myrtle Beach concentrates vacation rentals in its resort and oceanfront zoning districts and restricts them in many single-family residential zones, and individual buildings layer their own rules through the master deed and HOA. The practical takeaway: confirm both the zoning and the building's rental rules for the exact address before you write an offer, never after.

## How rental returns work in Myrtle Beach
On an oceanfront condo, returns start with gross rental revenue, but the number that matters is what is left after the building takes its share. Cleaning and turnover, the management split, HOA dues, accommodations taxes, and utilities commonly absorb 45 to 60 percent of gross before debt service. Estimate net operating income and a realistic annual occupancy, not the headline summer weeks, and deals that look average on gross often separate sharply on net. Cap rate and cash-on-cash return, run on conservative numbers, are the honest way to compare one building against another.

## Financing an investment property in Myrtle Beach
Financing is where oceanfront gets specific. Many resort condos are classified as condotels, which means larger down payments, higher rates, and fewer willing lenders. Warrantability, owner-occupancy ratios, reserve health, and litigation status all affect whether a conventional loan is even available. A lender who has financed these buildings before can flag which ones close cleanly and which will cost you a deal, before you spend on an inspection.

## Myrtle Beach rules and costs that move the numbers
Two cost levers move a Myrtle Beach pro forma more than buyers expect. First, South Carolina assesses non-owner-occupied property at a 6 percent ratio rather than the 4 percent applied to a primary residence, so the tax line on an investment condo runs materially higher. Confirm the current millage and ratio for the exact parcel. Second, short-term rentals collect and remit state and local accommodations and hospitality taxes, and the city requires a business license and a permit. Build both into the model from day one. Older oceanfront buildings also carry special-assessment risk, which is why the reserve study deserves as much attention as the rental history.

## The Myrtle Beach investor thesis

- 01 Oceanfront studios and one-bedrooms inside an established rental program are the lowest-friction entry to Myrtle Beach short-term rental investing.

- 02 Building-level rental history matters more than unit-level finishes. Analyze the building, then the unit.

- 03 Confirm City of Myrtle Beach zoning and the building's master deed before you offer. Not every address is short-term-rental eligible.

- 04 Inland single-family in Carolina Forest and The Market Common offers a steadier long-term-rental alternative when you want less seasonality.

## What a first Myrtle Beach deal looks like
A realistic first Myrtle Beach deal is an oceanfront studio or one-bedroom in a building with a documented rental program. The work happens before the offer: pull two or three years of the building's rental revenue, read the HOA budget and reserve study, confirm the unit's short-term-rental eligibility under both city zoning and the master deed, and verify condotel status with a lender so financing is locked. Buyers who do that homework can compare two similar-looking units and know which one actually nets more. The ones who skip it inherit a special assessment or a soft rental program they never priced in.

## What to watch before you buy in Myrtle Beach

- Condotel financing. Many oceanfront condos are classified as condotels, which means larger down payments and a shorter list of willing lenders. Line up financing before you shop.

- Special assessments. Older oceanfront buildings face salt-air maintenance, elevator and balcony repairs, and reserve shortfalls. Read the budget and reserve study, not just the listing.

- HOA rental rules. Some buildings cap rental frequency or require you to use the on-site program. That changes your numbers materially.

## Where Myrtle Beach sits, and how it is governed
Myrtle Beach is the hub of the Grand Strand, an incorporated city of roughly 35,000 residents in Horry County anchoring about 60 miles of Atlantic coastline. Myrtle Beach International Airport sits inside the city, which is unusual for a beach town and a real convenience for out-of-state owners. Because it is an incorporated city, the City of Myrtle Beach sets its own zoning and short-term-rental rules, which are stricter than the surrounding unincorporated county.

## The Myrtle Beach market right now
Myrtle Beach is a condo-heavy market, so a single median can mislead. City-wide figures land anywhere from the high $180,000s to the mid $310,000s depending on the source, because condos pull the number down and single-family homes push it up. As a reference point, Zillow put the city home-value index near $315,000 in early 2026, down about 3 percent year over year, while single-family homes commonly run in the $330,000s to high $380,000s and the ZIP codes range from about $275,000 in 29577 to about $354,000 in 29579. The condo segment carries the most inventory and the most negotiating room. For an accurate figure on the exact segment you want, we pull the Coastal Carolinas MLS.

## Short-term rental rules in the City of Myrtle Beach
This is the single most important thing an investor needs to know about Myrtle Beach, and most get it wrong: the city prohibits short-term rentals in nearly all traditional residential neighborhoods. Every zoning district beginning with R is off-limits for rentals under 90 days, with the lone exception of the RMV (Residential Multifamily Visitor) zone, and fewer than 30 grandfathered houses exist citywide. The city defines short-term as under 90 days (not the state 30) and treats STRs as a commercial use, requiring a business license and a 10 percent lodging tax. See the City of Myrtle Beach short-term rental guidance . If your plan is nightly rental income, you must buy in an STR-eligible zone (tourist-commercial or RMV) or a designated resort building, not a random R-zoned house. Every jurisdiction's licenses and taxes: short-term rental rules by city .

## What it costs to own in Myrtle Beach: the 4 percent versus 6 percent property tax rule
South Carolina assesses an owner-occupied primary residence at a 4 percent ratio with the owner-occupant school-operating credit, and a second home or investment property at 6 percent with no credit, so the effective property tax on the same home can run close to double when it is not your primary residence. After Horry County millage, effective rates typically land in the roughly 0.35 to 0.53 percent of market value range depending on use and location. See the South Carolina Department of Revenue for the assessment-ratio rules. Full county math, with a calculator: Horry County property taxes .

## Flood zones and insurance in Myrtle Beach
Flood exposure depends heavily on how close a property sits to the ocean, the Intracoastal Waterway, or low-lying inland pockets. Homes inside a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area generally require flood insurance on a federally backed loan, and coastal wind coverage has gotten more expensive across the Grand Strand. Chapter3 will pull the FEMA flood map for the specific address before you assume anything. What the three coastal policies cost: coastal home insurance costs .

## Myrtle Beach lifestyle and amenities
Myrtle Beach is the entertainment core of the Strand: the oceanfront Boardwalk and Promenade, the SkyWheel, Broadway at the Beach, Market Common (a walkable town-center district built on the old air-force base), Grande Dunes on the Intracoastal, and one of the densest concentrations of golf in the country. Everyday retail, healthcare, and dining are more built-out here than anywhere else on the Strand, and the airport is minutes from most neighborhoods.

## Schools serving Myrtle Beach
Public schools in the city fall within the Myrtle Beach attendance area of Horry County Schools , including Myrtle Beach Elementary, Middle, and High, along with other schools serving specific neighborhoods. Assignment is by address, and Chapter3 will confirm the exact schools for any property against the district attendance-boundary map.

## What it is like to live in Myrtle Beach
Living in the city itself, day-to-day life is more built-out than anywhere on the Strand: walkable town-center living at Market Common (a district built on the old air-force base), the oceanfront Boardwalk, Broadway at the Beach, and dense retail, dining, and healthcare. Myrtle Beach International Airport is minutes from most neighborhoods, which is unusual for a beach town. The tradeoff is summer traffic and crowds near the oceanfront core.
For a live-in buyer, the R-zoned residential neighborhoods (where short-term rentals are not allowed anyway) tend to be quieter and more year-round, while the tourist corridors stay busy in season. Check the flood zone and insurance for the exact address, and on a condo, the regime fees and reserve study.

## Buying in Myrtle Beach to live, not just to rent
Myrtle Beach is written about as an investor market, but plenty of buyers want a primary residence or a walkable second home here, and for them the STR ban in residential zones is a feature, not a bug: it keeps R-zoned neighborhoods residential. Weigh Market Common versus a resort community versus an established inland neighborhood, and remember a primary residence is taxed at 4% with the owner-occupant credit while a second home is 6% without it.

## Read the Myrtle Beach HOA rules before you commit to a house
In a market with this many associations, the covenants matter as much as the house. Before you make an offer, read the HOA bylaws and rules, because they can restrict short-term and long-term rentals, pets, parking, golf carts, fences, and exterior changes. The classic trap: you have spent years training your dog to walk off leash, then buy into a community with a strict leash rule and lose the thing you valued most. Read the documents before you make an offer, not after.
Ask us and we will get you the governing documents for any Myrtle Beach community, from our own files if we already have them or by requesting them for you if we do not. It is also why a Chapter3 agent asks a lot of questions about how you actually live: we would rather spend the time up front than match you to a home with a rule or an HOA that blocks what you enjoy or turns out to be a poor investment.

## Who Myrtle Beach suits
Myrtle Beach rewards two very different buyers. The first is a condo or resort investor who buys specifically in an STR-eligible zone and runs nightly rentals with the amenities and foot traffic the core provides. The second is a primary resident or second-home owner who wants walkable town-center living (Market Common) or an amenity-rich resort community and is not counting on STR income from an R-zoned house. If you want a single-family house to Airbnb, the city is usually the wrong target and an unincorporated oceanfront submarket like Garden City is the right one. We will steer you to the correct zone rather than let you buy a rental you cannot legally rent.

Myrtle Beach is the core of the Grand Strand and carries its deepest tourist demand. Inventory ranges widely, from oceanfront and resort condominiums to single-family neighborhoods further inland, which gives investors the broadest set of price points and strategies in the region.

Common Questions

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you short-term rental (Airbnb) a house in Myrtle Beach?
Usually not. The City of Myrtle Beach prohibits rentals under 90 days in all R (residential) zoning districts except RMV, and treats STRs as a commercial use. You generally need a property in an STR-eligible tourist or RMV zone, plus a business license and the 10 percent lodging tax.

### What counts as a short-term rental in Myrtle Beach?
The city defines a short-term rental as any stay under 90 days, which is stricter than South Carolina's general 30-day threshold.

### Is Myrtle Beach a buyer's or seller's market?
It leans toward buyers in early-to-mid 2026, especially in the condo segment, where inventory sits around seven to eight months of supply and gives buyers negotiating room.

### What are property taxes on a second home in Myrtle Beach?
Higher than on a primary residence. South Carolina assesses primary homes at a 4 percent ratio with a school-tax credit and second homes or investments at 6 percent with no credit, so the effective tax on the same home can be close to double.

### Which schools serve Myrtle Beach?
Public schools fall within the Myrtle Beach attendance area of Horry County Schools. Assignment is by address, and Chapter3 will confirm the exact schools on the district boundary map.

### Is Myrtle Beach good for short-term rentals?
It has the region&#x27;s deepest tourist demand, especially near the oceanfront, though performance and short-term-rental rules vary by area and building.

### What property types are common in Myrtle Beach?
A broad mix, from oceanfront and resort condominiums to single-family neighborhoods inland.

# North Myrtle Beach Real Estate Investing
North Myrtle Beach is the family-beach short-term rental market: medians roughly $399,000 to $415,000, rentals allowed citywide, and a licensing regime still in draft.

## Real estate investing in North Myrtle Beach, SC
North Myrtle Beach is the Grand Strand's family-and-golf beach. Made up of the historic sections of Cherry Grove, Ocean Drive, Crescent Beach, and Windy Hill, it draws repeat vacationers who return to the same streets year after year. That repeat demand gives the short-term rental market a steadier, more loyal base than the high-churn Myrtle Beach strip, and it supports a higher-end inventory of beach houses alongside the condos.
The city is its own municipality with its own character. It is quieter and more residential than Myrtle Beach, leans toward families and golfers rather than the boardwalk crowd, and includes the Ocean Drive section that anchors the region's shag-dancing culture and its spring and fall SOS festivals, which extend the rental calendar into the shoulder seasons.

## North Myrtle Beach property types and pricing
North Myrtle Beach offers a genuinely mixed inventory: oceanfront and second-row condos, channel and canal homes in Cherry Grove with private docks, and larger single-family beach houses that sleep ten or more and command strong weekly rates in summer. The larger homes carry higher entry prices but can produce outsized peak-season revenue when they are positioned for big family groups.
Cherry Grove's tidal channels are a distinct niche. Homes on the channels offer boat and fishing access that pure beach blocks do not, and that feature carries its own demand from a specific buyer and renter. Pricing across the city runs from entry condos into the multi-million-dollar range for prime oceanfront houses.

## Where investors are looking in North Myrtle Beach
The city's four historic sections each behave a little differently. Cherry Grove draws investors to its tidal channels, where dock access commands a premium. Ocean Drive is the walkable, festival-anchored core with steady repeat demand. Crescent Beach and Windy Hill round out the oceanfront with a mix of condos and houses. Just inland, Barefoot Resort along the Intracoastal Waterway adds golf-community and waterway inventory that broadens the buyer pool beyond pure beach product.

## The North Myrtle Beach rental market
Short-term rental is well established and broadly accepted here, which is part of the appeal: it is a purpose-built vacation market rather than a residential one fighting over rental rights. The larger beach houses in particular benefit from group travel, where a single booking covers what several condo bookings would. Long-term rental exists but is secondary to vacation rental.
As everywhere on the Strand, the specifics still matter. HOA rules vary building to building and community to community, and the city administers business licensing and accommodations tax on short-term rentals. The seasonal revenue curve mirrors the regional pattern, with the shag festivals adding useful shoulder-season pop that the pure-summer markets lack.

## How rental returns work in North Myrtle Beach
Returns on the larger beach houses are a revenue-per-booking story. A single group rental can cover what several condo bookings would, but the expense load is real: professional cleaning of a large home, landscaping, pool service where applicable, and management. Run the full-year net, not the summer gross, and weigh peak weekly rates against the slower months. The houses that clear the best returns are the ones positioned for big families and reviewed well enough to earn repeat bookings.

## Financing an investment property in North Myrtle Beach
Single-family beach houses generally finance more conventionally than condotels, which is part of their appeal, but second-home and investment-property loans still carry higher down payments and rates than a primary residence. DSCR financing, which qualifies on the property's rental income rather than your personal income, is a common path for investors here. Line up the loan type before you shop so your offer is credible.

## North Myrtle Beach rules and costs that move the numbers
Budget for the rules and the taxes, not just the mortgage. South Carolina taxes non-owner-occupied property at a 6 percent assessment ratio versus 4 percent for a primary residence, so an investment beach house carries a heavier tax line. Confirm the current rate for the parcel. Short-term rentals also remit state and local accommodations taxes and need proper licensing. On top of that, oceanfront and Cherry Grove channel homes sit in flood zones, so a real flood-insurance quote belongs in your numbers before you fall for the view.

## The North Myrtle Beach investor thesis

- 01 Larger beach houses positioned for family groups can outproduce condos on peak-season revenue per booking.

- 02 Cherry Grove channel homes are a defensible niche: dock access draws renters and buyers that beach-block inventory cannot.

- 03 Repeat, loyalty-driven demand makes revenue here steadier and easier to forecast than the high-churn strip.

- 04 Golf and shag-festival demand lengthens the rental calendar into spring and fall.

## What a first North Myrtle Beach deal looks like
A common first move here is a three or four-bedroom beach house positioned for family groups, bought with a clear-eyed view of the full-year calendar. Estimate the slow months, not just peak summer, confirm the community allows the rental frequency you need, get the elevation certificate and a real flood quote, and price in professional cleaning and management for a larger home. A well-reviewed house that sleeps a big group can outproduce two condos, but only when the operating costs were in the model from the start.

## What to watch before you buy in North Myrtle Beach

- Entry price on houses. The big beach houses cost more up front, so peak revenue has to carry more property. Estimate the full year, not just July.

- Flood and elevation. Cherry Grove and oceanfront blocks sit in flood zones. Get the elevation certificate and a real insurance quote before you commit.

- HOA and community rules. Some communities restrict rentals or short minimum stays. Confirm per address.

## Where North Myrtle Beach sits, and how it is governed
North Myrtle Beach is an incorporated Horry County city of roughly 17,000 to 18,000 residents, formed in 1968 by merging four beach communities that people still use as neighborhood names: Cherry Grove, Ocean Drive, Crescent Beach, and Windy Hill. Because it is its own city, it runs its own short-term-rental permitting, which is more structured than the surrounding county.

## The North Myrtle Beach market right now
Median sale prices ran roughly $399,000 to $415,000 in early 2026 per Redfin and Zillow, trending a few percent below the 2025 peak. The internal spread is wide: two-bedroom condos start in the $200,000s and around a $268,000 median, while single-family homes carry a much higher median (well into the $600,000s), and Cherry Grove oceanfront and canal homes routinely exceed $1 million. Treat the headline median as a blend and price by segment and section.

## Short-term rental rules in North Myrtle Beach
North Myrtle Beach allows short-term rentals but regulates them actively. Operators need an annual short-term-rental permit and a business license, the property must pass a physical and fire-safety inspection, and every rental must have a Responsible Local Agent on file. An owner can serve as their own agent only if they live within 30 miles; otherwise they must appoint a licensed property manager or brokerage, which matters for out-of-state buyers. Rentals are limited to specific zones (resort-residential and similar), and an HOA can add its own limits. See the North Myrtle Beach code of ordinances . If you are not sure who you could name as your responsible local agent, talk to your Chapter3 agent; we can serve in that role or connect you with a licensed local manager who meets the city requirement. Every jurisdiction's licenses and taxes: short-term rental rules by city .

## What it costs to own in North Myrtle Beach: the 4 percent versus 6 percent property tax rule
South Carolina assesses an owner-occupied primary residence at a 4 percent ratio with the owner-occupant school credit, and a second home or investment at 6 percent with no credit, so the effective property tax on the same home can be close to double when it is not your primary residence. See the South Carolina Department of Revenue for the assessment-ratio rules. Full county math, with a calculator: Horry County property taxes .

## Flood zones and insurance in North Myrtle Beach
Flood risk is a core cost factor on the North Strand. Public First Street data reported by Redfin flags a large share of North Myrtle Beach properties (around 44 percent) as facing elevated flood risk over a 30-year horizon, and Cherry Grove's canals and marsh edges carry particular exposure. Pull the FEMA flood map and, on low-lying or oceanfront lots, an elevation certificate before you commit. What the three coastal policies cost: coastal home insurance costs .

## North Myrtle Beach lifestyle and amenities
North Myrtle Beach has a distinct identity from Myrtle Beach: Ocean Drive is the home of the shag (the state dance) and a walkable Main Street, Cherry Grove offers a fishing pier and a wide tidal marsh, and Barefoot Resort brings four championship golf courses and a marina on the Intracoastal. McLeod Seacoast provides local hospital care, and the overall feel is more residential and family-oriented than the entertainment core to the south.

## Schools serving North Myrtle Beach
Public schools fall within the North Myrtle Beach attendance area of Horry County Schools , including Ocean Drive Elementary, North Myrtle Beach Middle, and North Myrtle Beach High. Assignment is by address, and Chapter3 will confirm the exact schools for any property against the district attendance-boundary map.
Chapter3 does not rate schools as good or bad; that is your call to make from the full record. The honest way to research a school is to read the official, neutral sources directly: the South Carolina Department of Education school report cards publish state accountability ratings, test performance, and graduation data for every public school, and GreatSchools aggregates ratings and parent reviews. Read both, visit the school, and talk to families in the specific attendance zone. The report card also publishes SAT and ACT averages, Advanced Placement and dual-enrollment participation, college-and-career readiness, dropout rate, and chronic absenteeism. Ask your Chapter3 agent and we will pull the report card and enrollment details for any address alongside you.

## Buying in North Myrtle Beach to live, not just to rent
Most of what is written about North Myrtle Beach is aimed at investors, but a large share of buyers here want a primary residence or a second home, and the questions are different. If you are buying to live, weigh the year-round feel of the section you choose (Ocean Drive has a walkable Main Street and shag-dancing culture, Cherry Grove is quieter and marsh-facing), golf-cart access, proximity to McLeod Seacoast for healthcare, and how seasonal the street gets in summer. Condo buyers should scrutinize the regime (HOA) fees and the reserve study, because coastal insurance has pushed dues and special assessments up across the Strand.
The primary-versus-second-home decision also changes your tax bill directly: a primary residence is assessed at South Carolina's 4 percent ratio with the owner-occupant school credit, while a second home is assessed at 6 percent with no credit, so budget for the higher effective rate if this will not be your full-time home. For a live-in buyer, resale, walkability, flood elevation, and HOA rules usually matter more than nightly-rate projections, and we weight the search accordingly.

## Read the North Myrtle Beach HOA rules before you commit to a house
In a market this HOA-heavy, the covenants matter as much as the house. Before you make an offer, read the association's bylaws and rules, because they can restrict short-term and long-term rentals, pets, parking, golf carts, fences, exterior changes, and more. The classic trap: you have spent years training your dog to walk off leash, then buy into a community with a strict leash rule and lose the thing you valued most. That is a fixable mistake if you catch it before closing and an expensive one if you do not.
Ask us and we will get you the governing documents for any community, from our own files if we already have them or by requesting them for you if we do not, so you read the real rules and not a listing summary. It is also why, when you call a Chapter3 agent, we ask a lot of questions about you and how you actually live. We would rather spend the extra time up front than match you to a home with a rule or an HOA that blocks what you enjoy or turns out to be a poor investment.

## What it is like to live in North Myrtle Beach
For a primary residence or a full-time second home, the day-to-day here is quieter and more settled than the Myrtle Beach core. Ocean Drive has an actual walkable Main Street and is the historic home of the shag, South Carolina's state dance, so there is a real downtown to live near rather than just a strip of rentals. Cherry Grove, at the north end, is calmer and marsh-facing, with a fishing pier and tidal creeks instead of nightlife. Golf carts are a normal way to get around; South Carolina allows registered carts on secondary roads in daylight within a few miles of home.
Everyday life is well covered: grocery and retail along Highway 17, four championship courses and a marina at Barefoot Resort, and McLeod Seacoast for hospital care. Commutes are short for residents who work locally, and the community feels genuinely year-round outside the summer peak. As a live-in buyer, the things worth checking before you fall for a house are the flood elevation and insurance cost for the exact lot, the regime or HOA dues and reserve study on a condo, and the community rules covered below, rather than nightly-rate projections. Those are the numbers that shape daily life here.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do you need a permit to short-term rental in North Myrtle Beach?
Yes. The city requires an annual short-term-rental permit and a business license, a safety inspection, and a Responsible Local Agent on file. Owners who live more than 30 miles away must appoint a licensed local property manager or brokerage as that agent.

### Can an out-of-state owner run an Airbnb in North Myrtle Beach?
Yes, but you must appoint a Responsible Local Agent within 30 miles of the property, so most out-of-state owners hire a licensed local manager or brokerage to meet the requirement.

### What are the neighborhoods in North Myrtle Beach?
The city formed in 1968 from four communities still used as area names: Cherry Grove, Ocean Drive, Crescent Beach, and Windy Hill, plus resort communities like Barefoot Resort.

### What are property taxes on a second home in North Myrtle Beach?
South Carolina assesses primary homes at 4 percent with a school-tax credit and second homes or investments at 6 percent with no credit, so the effective tax on the same home can be close to double.

### Which schools serve North Myrtle Beach?
Public schools fall within the North Myrtle Beach attendance area of Horry County Schools. Chapter3 will confirm the exact assignment for an address on the district boundary map.

### Is North Myrtle Beach better for families?
It is known for a quieter, family oriented feel than central Myrtle Beach while still offering steady vacation-rental demand.

### How is vacation-rental demand in North Myrtle Beach?
Established and steady, particularly in beach proximate communities like Cherry Grove and Ocean Drive.

## Real estate investing in Pawleys Island, SC
Pawleys Island is the Grand Strand's historic, understated luxury market. Self-described as arrogantly shabby, it trades on old beach houses, low density, mature live oaks, and a deliberate resistance to commercialization. The market extends from the narrow barrier island itself to the mainland communities of Litchfield and the prestigious golf clubs at Caledonia and True Blue. This is second-home and luxury territory, not entry-level investing.
Buyers here are typically affluent second-home owners and a smaller set of luxury short-term-rental investors. The appeal is exclusivity and scarcity: the island has limited inventory, strict character, and a buyer pool willing to pay for it. That keeps the floor under values but also raises the entry price well above the northern Strand.

## Pawleys Island property types and pricing
The signature property is the classic Pawleys beach house, often older and characterful, on or near the ocean or creek. Inland, Litchfield and the golf communities offer single-family homes and some villas at a range of price points, generally above the regional median. Entry to the island itself starts high and climbs quickly for oceanfront.
Scarcity is the defining economic feature. Limited supply and protected character mean the market does not flood with inventory, which supports values but also means patience is required to find the right asset.

## Where investors are looking in Pawleys Island
The barrier island itself holds the classic oceanfront and creek-side beach houses at the top of the market. On the mainland, Litchfield Beach and Litchfield by the Sea offer a mix of homes and villas with beach access. The prestigious golf communities, Caledonia, True Blue, Pawleys Plantation, and Willbrook, draw golf-trip rental demand and a deep second-home buyer pool, often at more attainable price points than the island.

## The Pawleys Island rental market
Short-term rental here is a luxury, lower-volume, higher-rate business rather than a high-occupancy churn model. Well-positioned beach houses command strong weekly rates from a discerning renter, and the golf communities draw golf-trip demand. Long-term and seasonal rental also exist for the second-home set. Rules vary between the Town of Pawleys Island on the barrier island and the surrounding unincorporated Georgetown County, and the island's character-protective posture means rental specifics must be confirmed carefully per address.

## How rental returns work in Pawleys Island
Luxury changes the return equation. Occupancy runs lower than the high-volume beach towns, but weekly rates on a well-positioned beach house are far higher, and the buyer is often as motivated by appreciation and personal use as by yield. Estimate a realistic luxury occupancy, account for the heavier upkeep of an older high-end home, and treat strong appreciation potential as part of the total return rather than relying on cash flow alone.

## Financing an investment property in Pawleys Island
Higher price points mean jumbo financing enters the picture on many island and luxury properties, with stricter reserve and documentation requirements. Second-home loans are common given the buyer profile. For income properties, DSCR financing works but the lower occupancy of a luxury rental affects the coverage calculation, so the estimate has to be realistic about achievable rents.

## Pawleys Island rules and costs that move the numbers
At Pawleys price points, the cost lines carry weight. South Carolina's 6 percent assessment ratio on non-owner-occupied property, applied to a higher-value home, produces a substantial tax bill, and Chapter3 will confirm it early. Oceanfront and creek-side properties on or near the island need serious wind and flood coverage, which is a recurring cost worth quoting before you offer. Short-term luxury rentals also remit state and local accommodations taxes. On an appreciation-driven luxury asset, these carrying costs are the difference between a comfortable hold and a strained one.

## The Pawleys Island investor thesis

- 01 This is a scarcity-and-luxury play: limited supply and protected character support values over time.

- 02 Premium weekly rates on well-positioned beach houses can outweigh lower occupancy in a luxury model.

- 03 Litchfield and the Caledonia and True Blue golf communities add golf-trip rental demand and a deep second-home buyer pool.

- 04 Patience pays. The right asset is worth waiting for in a thin-inventory market.

## What a first Pawleys Island deal looks like
A first Pawleys investment is rarely an entry-level move, so the realistic version is often a Litchfield or golf-community home rather than oceanfront on the island itself. These carry more attainable price points while still drawing golf-trip rental demand and a deep second-home buyer pool. Estimate luxury-market occupancy, budget honestly for the upkeep of an older or higher-end home, and treat appreciation and personal use as part of the return. Patience matters here: thin inventory means the right asset is worth waiting for.

## What to watch before you buy in Pawleys Island

- High entry price. Capital requirements are well above the northern Strand. Returns lean on appreciation and premium rates, not volume.

- Older-home maintenance. Classic beach houses carry real upkeep. Inspect thoroughly and budget for it.

- Town versus county rules. The barrier island and the mainland follow different jurisdictions and rental rules. Confirm for the exact address.

## Where Pawleys Island sits, and how it is governed
Pawleys Island is a Georgetown County market about 25 miles south of Myrtle Beach and one of the oldest summer resorts on the East Coast, known for its understated "arrogantly shabby" character. It has two parts that matter for buyers: the small incorporated Town of Pawleys Island (the barrier island itself, a tiny town) and the larger unincorporated mainland, which includes Litchfield, Pawleys Plantation, Hagley Estates, The River Club, and, to the south, gated DeBordieu Colony.

## The Pawleys Island market right now
Pawleys Island is the upscale end of the southern Strand. Zillow's home-value index sat near $514,000 in mid-2026 (up about 5 percent year over year), and other trackers put the median list price in the mid $500,000s, with waterfront and gated-community homes running well higher and DeBordieu reaching into the multi-millions. See the Zillow Pawleys Island home values . Small-sample monthly medians can swing hard here, so treat any single month with caution and price by community.

## Short-term rental rules in Pawleys Island
Short-term rentals are generally allowed in the Pawleys Island area, and there is no permanent ban; the only documented prohibition was a temporary COVID-era emergency ordinance in 2020. Rules differ by jurisdiction: the incorporated Town of Pawleys Island governs the barrier island, while mainland communities fall under Georgetown County zoning. See Georgetown County zoning . On top of that, gated communities like Pawleys Plantation and DeBordieu have their own governing documents that can restrict rentals, and Chapter3 will verify both the jurisdiction and the HOA for a specific address. Every jurisdiction's licenses and taxes: short-term rental rules by city .

## What it costs to own in Pawleys Island: the 4 percent versus 6 percent property tax rule
South Carolina assesses an owner-occupied primary residence at a 4 percent ratio with the owner-occupant school credit, and a second home or investment at 6 percent with no credit, so the effective property tax on the same home can be close to double when it is not your primary residence. Georgetown County's combined sales tax is 7 percent. See the South Carolina Department of Revenue for the assessment-ratio rules. Full county math, with a calculator: Horry County property taxes .

## Flood zones and insurance in Pawleys Island
Flood exposure is high and central to buying here, because much of the market is on or near a barrier island and tidal creeks. Public First Street data reported by Redfin flags an extreme share of Pawleys Island properties (around 89 percent) as facing severe flood risk over 30 years, and essentially the entire area carries elevated wind risk. Flood insurance and elevation certificates are not optional details here; get them for the specific address early. What the three coastal policies cost: coastal home insurance costs .

## Pawleys Island lifestyle and amenities
Pawleys Island trades nightlife for nature and history: quiet beaches, salt-marsh creeks, surfing and sea-turtle nesting, a historic district dating to the 1700s, and Jack Nicklaus-designed golf at Pawleys Plantation. Brookgreen Gardens and Huntington Beach State Park are just north, dining and shopping run along the Ocean Highway (U.S. 17) on the mainland, and the pace is deliberately slower than the rest of the Strand.

## Schools serving Pawleys Island
Public schools fall within the Georgetown County School District, generally the Waccamaw schools (Waccamaw Elementary, Waccamaw Intermediate, Waccamaw Middle, and Waccamaw High) for the Litchfield and Pawleys area. Private options include Lowcountry Preparatory School. Assignment is by address, and Chapter3 will confirm the exact schools on the district boundary map.

## What it is like to live in Pawleys Island
Pawleys Island trades nightlife for nature and history: quiet beaches, salt-marsh creeks, a historic district dating to the 1700s, and an understated, "arrogantly shabby" character. Brookgreen Gardens and Huntington Beach State Park are just north, dining and shopping run along Ocean Highway on the mainland, and the pace is deliberately slower than the rest of the Strand.
For a live-in buyer, flood is central: much of the market is on or near a barrier island and tidal creeks, so flood insurance and an elevation certificate are essential for any purchase. Georgetown County property tax runs low relative to the national average, and the area skews toward higher-end, gated, and golf communities.

## Buying in Pawleys Island to live, not just to rent
Pawleys is the upscale, lifestyle end of the southern Strand, and many buyers here want a primary residence or a quiet second home rather than a rental. It suits patient, lifestyle-driven buyers who want understated and established over entertainment and volume, including luxury buyers in gated communities like Pawleys Plantation or DeBordieu. A primary residence is taxed at 4% with the owner-occupant credit; a second home at 6% without it.

## Read the Pawleys Island HOA rules before you commit to a house
In a market with this many associations, the covenants matter as much as the house. Before you make an offer, read the HOA bylaws and rules, because they can restrict short-term and long-term rentals, pets, parking, golf carts, fences, and exterior changes. The classic trap: you have spent years training your dog to walk off leash, then buy into a community with a strict leash rule and lose the thing you valued most. Read the documents before you make an offer, not after.
Ask us and we will get you the governing documents for any Pawleys Island community, from our own files if we already have them or by requesting them for you if we do not. It is also why a Chapter3 agent asks a lot of questions about how you actually live: we would rather spend the time up front than match you to a home with a rule or an HOA that blocks what you enjoy or turns out to be a poor investment.

# Surfside Beach Real Estate Investing
Surfside Beach is a small family beach town where oceanfront medians run into the $800,000s while typical home values sit near $347,000 to $360,000, and short-term rentals are limited to two zoning districts.

## Real estate investing in Surfside Beach, SC
Surfside Beach markets itself as The Family Beach, and the branding is accurate. It is a small, incorporated town with a quieter, lower-key feel than Myrtle Beach, a mix of beach cottages, condos, and single-family homes, and a reputation for families who want the coast without the crowds and neon. That positioning supports both a healthy short-term rental market and a real base of year-round residents.
Because Surfside has a genuine local population, it is one of the more balanced submarkets on the Strand. An investor can run a beach cottage as a vacation rental, hold a single-family home as a long-term rental for local tenants, or pursue the snowbird hybrid that fills winter months with monthly renters. That optionality lowers risk relative to the pure-tourism corridors.

## Surfside Beach property types and pricing
Inventory ranges from older raised beach cottages near the ocean to newer single-family homes and townhomes set back from the water, plus a stock of mid-rise condos. The closer to the beach, the more the property leans short-term; the further back, the more it behaves like a conventional residential rental. Entry pricing is generally more approachable than the prime oceanfront corridors, which is part of the appeal for first-time investors.
The town's manageable scale is a feature. It is walkable, the pier is a focal point, and renters value the calmer atmosphere, which translates into loyal repeat bookings for well-kept properties.

## Where investors are looking in Surfside Beach
The closer to the pier and the ocean, the stronger the short-term-rental case, and the original beach cottage blocks are where vacation demand concentrates. Set back from the water, conventional subdivisions and the Deerfield golf community support long-term rentals to local tenants. Ocean Lakes, the large leasehold beachfront community nearby, is a distinct niche with its own ownership structure that investors should understand before buying in.

## The Surfside Beach rental market
Short-term rental works well near the beach, and the family positioning supports strong summer occupancy and repeat guests. Away from the immediate beach, long-term rental to local tenants is a viable and lower-volatility path. The town administers its own business licensing and accommodations requirements, and as a municipality it can set rules that differ from the unincorporated county around it, and Chapter3 will confirm the rules for the specific street.

## How rental returns work in Surfside Beach
Because Surfside supports both strategies, the return math splits two ways. Near the beach, model it like a vacation rental: gross revenue less cleaning, management, and seasonal vacancy. Set back from the water, model it like a long-term hold: monthly rent less the 35 to 45 percent that taxes, insurance, maintenance, and management typically absorb. The more approachable entry pricing here means cash-on-cash returns can pencil even on conservative rent assumptions.

## Financing an investment property in Surfside Beach
Conventional single-family homes here finance straightforwardly, while condos depend on the project's warrantability and HOA health. For the long-term-rental side, DSCR loans that qualify on rent are a clean fit. Confirm condo-project approval early if you are buying in a building, since a non-warrantable project narrows your lender options considerably.

## Surfside Beach rules and costs that move the numbers
A few local costs shape the math. Non-owner-occupied property is assessed at South Carolina's 6 percent ratio rather than the 4 percent primary-residence ratio, and Chapter3 will verify the tax line for the address. If you run the property as a short-term rental, the town requires licensing and the usual state and local accommodations taxes apply. Near-beach cottages also need a genuine flood-insurance quote. None of these are deal-killers, but they separate a pro forma that holds up from one that looks good only until the first tax bill.

## The Surfside Beach investor thesis

- 01 Balanced demand lets you choose strategy by property: vacation rental near the beach, long-term hold further back.

- 02 More approachable entry pricing than prime oceanfront makes Surfside a sensible first investment market.

- 03 The family brand drives loyal repeat bookings, which favors well-kept, well-reviewed properties.

- 04 The snowbird monthly-rental hybrid smooths winter vacancy without committing to year-round leasing.

## What a first Surfside Beach deal looks like
A sensible first Surfside deal often means choosing strategy by location. Near the beach, a cottage or condo run as a vacation rental; set back from the water, a single-family home held for a local long-term tenant. Either way, Chapter3 will confirm the town's licensing rules, verify condo-project warrantability if you are buying in a building, and run conservative rent or occupancy numbers with you. The more approachable entry pricing means a first deal here can cash-flow without heroic assumptions, which is exactly what a first investment should do.

## What to watch before you buy in Surfside Beach

- Older cottage condition. Many beach cottages are older raised structures. Budget for roof, HVAC, and elevation-related maintenance.

- Town rules. Surfside is incorporated and sets its own short-term-rental and licensing rules. Chapter3 will verify them for the exact address.

- Flood insurance. Near-beach properties need a real flood quote in your numbers, not a guess.

## Where Surfside Beach sits, and how it is governed
Surfside Beach is a small incorporated Horry County town just south of Myrtle Beach that brands itself "The Family Beach." It runs on golf carts as much as cars (South Carolina allows registered carts on secondary roads in daylight within a few miles of home), and because it is its own town it sets its own short-term-rental zoning, which is stricter than unincorporated areas nearby.

## The Surfside Beach market right now
Surfside is a two-tier market, so read the numbers carefully. A blended median can look high (Redfin reported around $530,000 in early 2026) because it mixes small inland condos with oceanfront homes, while detached single-family homes carry a much higher median (into the $800,000s) and the typical home-value index sits closer to the $347,000 to $360,000 range. Price per square foot averages around $322 town-wide but climbs toward $540 in ocean-adjacent corridors, and days on market have run near 108. Always separate the oceanfront tier from the inland tier.

## Short-term rental rules in Surfside Beach
Surfside Beach permits short-term rentals (under 30 days) only in specific zoning districts: the R3 high-density residential zone closer to the ocean and the C3 commercial zone. In the inland R1 low-density zones, transient rentals are restricted or prohibited. Operators need a town short-term-rental permit and must pass a safety inspection, and long-term rentals (a year or longer) are allowed in all residential zones. Verifying R3 versus R1 for a specific address before you write an offer is the single most expensive mistake buyers avoid here. Confirm current rules with the Town of Surfside Beach . Every jurisdiction's licenses and taxes: short-term rental rules by city .

## What it costs to own in Surfside Beach: the 4 percent versus 6 percent property tax rule
South Carolina assesses an owner-occupied primary residence at a 4 percent ratio with the owner-occupant school credit, and a second home or investment at 6 percent with no credit, so the effective property tax on the same home can be close to double when it is not your primary residence. See the South Carolina Department of Revenue for the assessment-ratio rules. Full county math, with a calculator: Horry County property taxes .

## Flood zones and insurance in Surfside Beach
Surfside enforces elevation requirements and participates in the FEMA Community Rating System, which can lower flood-insurance costs for compliant properties. Oceanfront and low-lying lots still carry meaningful flood and wind exposure. Review the FEMA flood map and, on ocean-adjacent lots, the elevation certificate before you buy, and on condos ask for the reserve study, since regime (HOA) fees have risen with coastal insurance costs. What the three coastal policies cost: coastal home insurance costs .

## Surfside Beach lifestyle and amenities
Surfside is deliberately low-key: a walkable downtown, the Surfside Pier, golf-cart access throughout, and a quieter, residential feel than Myrtle Beach. South Strand Medical Center is close by, and the Murrells Inlet MarshWalk dining scene is a short drive south, so residents get restaurants and nightlife without hosting the crowds themselves.

## Schools serving Surfside Beach
Public schools fall within Horry County Schools , with the area generally served by Lakewood Elementary, St. James Intermediate, and St. James High. Assignment is by address, and Chapter3 will confirm the exact schools on the district boundary map.

## What it is like to live in Surfside Beach
Surfside Beach is deliberately low-key: a small incorporated town that runs on golf carts, with a walkable downtown, the Surfside Pier, and a quieter, more residential feel than Myrtle Beach. South Carolina allows registered golf carts on secondary roads in daylight within a few miles of home, and residents get the Murrells Inlet MarshWalk dining scene a short drive south without hosting the crowds themselves.
For a live-in buyer, the inland R1 zones (where short-term rentals are restricted anyway) are quieter and more year-round, while the R3 zone near the ocean is busier in season. South Strand Medical Center is close, and the key checks are the flood zone and elevation for the exact lot and, on a condo, the regime fees and reserve study.

## Buying in Surfside Beach to live, not just to rent
Surfside brands itself "The Family Beach," and many buyers want a primary residence or a quiet second home rather than a rental. If that is you, an inland R1 property fits, and the short-term-rental restriction there is a plus for a residential street. A primary residence is taxed at 4% with the owner-occupant credit; a second home at 6% without it.

## Read the Surfside Beach HOA rules before you commit to a house
In a market with this many associations, the covenants matter as much as the house. Before you make an offer, read the HOA bylaws and rules, because they can restrict short-term and long-term rentals, pets, parking, golf carts, fences, and exterior changes. The classic trap: you have spent years training your dog to walk off leash, then buy into a community with a strict leash rule and lose the thing you valued most. Read the documents before you make an offer, not after.
Ask us and we will get you the governing documents for any Surfside Beach community, from our own files if we already have them or by requesting them for you if we do not. It is also why a Chapter3 agent asks a lot of questions about how you actually live: we would rather spend the time up front than match you to a home with a rule or an HOA that blocks what you enjoy or turns out to be a poor investment.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you Airbnb a property in Surfside Beach?
Only in the right zone. Surfside permits short-term rentals (under 30 days) in the R3 high-density and C3 commercial districts and restricts or prohibits them in inland R1 low-density zones. A town STR permit and safety inspection are required.

### Is Surfside Beach a golf-cart town?
Yes. Golf carts are a primary local mode of transport, and South Carolina allows registered carts on secondary roads during daylight within a few miles of home.

### Why do Surfside Beach median prices look so high?
Because the blended median mixes small inland condos with oceanfront homes. Detached single-family medians run much higher than the overall home-value index, so compare within a tier.

### What are property taxes on a second home in Surfside Beach?
South Carolina assesses primary homes at 4 percent with a school-tax credit and second homes or investments at 6 percent with no credit, so the effective tax on the same home can be close to double.

### Which schools serve Surfside Beach?
Public schools fall within Horry County Schools, generally Lakewood Elementary, St. James Intermediate, and St. James High. Chapter3 will confirm the exact assignment on the district boundary map.

### Why is Surfside Beach called the family beach?
It has a quieter, more residential feel than central Myrtle Beach, with steady seasonal demand and a mix of homes and condominiums.

### What does Surfside Beach offer investors?
A calmer setting close to the main attractions, with both single-family and condominium options.

## The building study we run before you offer

The heart of working with a Chapter3 agent is the study we run on any property you are serious about, before a cent of earnest money is on the line. It includes:

- The HOA bylaws and as many of the association’s financials as we can get our hands on.

- The building’s litigation history , where it is obtainable.

- A full investment analysis : long-term and short-term rent expectations, the average nightly rate, occupancy month by month, and every figure we can build from them, including net operating income (income left after expenses), cap rate (the yearly return if you paid all cash), cash-on-cash return (yearly cash profit divided by the cash you put in), and expected appreciation.

Even if you never intend to rent it out, that analysis tells you whether you are paying a fair price for what you are actually getting.

Here is the uncomfortable truth about real estate: most brokerages are interchangeable, and the quality you actually get swings wildly from one agent to the next. After the keys

Formulas vs. facts

Zillow and the portals run generic formulas, the same national math on every house, with no history of the specific property in front of you.
